title: Adapting the concept of embeddedness: Extending systemic B2B marketing theories in the Anthropocene
Science as a signal of expertise: adoption of AI recommendation in strategic decision-making among SMEs
Why do customers mistreat service employees? The roles of environmental noise, customer depletion, and restorative servicescapes
abstract: Purpose Customer mistreatment refers to customers' low-quality interpersonal treatment and unreasonable demands directed toward service employees. This study examines how environmental noise contributes to customer mistreatment of service employees. It further investigates whether restorative servicescapes mitigate this detrimental effect. Design/methodology/approach This research included three studies, each employing a distinct research design to empirically test the proposed model. Data were collected through field observations of 261 customer–employee interactions (Study 1), a field survey of 201 customer–employee encounters (Study 2), and retrospective experiences method from 356 customers (Study 3). Findings Across the three studies, the findings consistently show that: (1) noise from other customers indirectly increases customer mistreatment via customer ego depletion, and (2) restorative servicescapes mitigate this indirect effect. Originality/value Integrating the environmental psychology theories, this study finds that restorative servicescapes moderate the indirect effect of environmental noise on customer mistreatment. Incorporating this contextual moderator into the customer mistreatment literature not only clarifies its theoretical boundary conditions but also offers practical implications for service organizations.

title: Streaming anytime, anywhere but for the same reasons? A three-country study of mobile TV public and private usage
abstract: Purpose Research has not kept pace with the growing use of mobile TV and has yet to fully examine how this trend varies across countries. This study addresses this gap through two key aims. First, it examines how the factors associated with continued use of mobile TV differ between South Korea, the United States of America and Germany using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) framework. Second, it explores cross-national variations in the public and private usage of mobile TV. Design/methodology/approach The research employs an online survey conducted across three national samples: the USA (n = 308), Germany (n = 309) and South Korea (n = 342). Data are analysed using a combination of covariance-based structural equation modelling and binary logistic regression. Findings Findings reveal that hedonic motivation, price value and facilitating conditions are consistently associated with continued usage intentions. However, performance expectancy, effort expectancy and social influence within the UTAUT2 framework show varying associations, with notably stronger associations observed in South Korea. For usage, hedonic motivation is significantly associated with private but not with public usage. Originality/value This research contributes to the emerging field of mobile TV usage, which, despite rapid growth, remains underexplored in academic literature. It also adds value by comparing three distinct international markets, an uncommon approach in technology adoption research. Furthermore, it highlights the yet to be considered public and private usage of mobile TV technology.

title: Strategic fit and new venture performance in global breadth-oriented digital corporate accelerators
The inverted U-shaped effect of artificial intelligence orientation on startup fundraising: a focus on the defense sector
Towards a better understanding of the initiation process for new university-industry relationships: the role of interpersonal dynamics in collaborative innovation projects
abstract: Abstract While significant research has focused on how relationships between universities and industry develop, little is known about the initiation stage and the micro-level interpersonal dynamics that underpin it. This stage is critical: it strongly influences whether a relationship is founded and shapes its subsequent success or failure. We identify and conceptualize the behaviours of boundary-spanning individuals (innovation champions) that support relationship initiation or contribute to premature termination. Participants described preparation, responsiveness, follow-through, and resource investment as influencing their assessments of prospective partners and their decisions about whether to continue relationship development. Using signalling theory abductively, we interpret these observable behaviours as potential signals through which champions and prospective partners may update their beliefs about one another’s otherwise unobservable latent commitment. On this basis, we extend the literature by developing an exploratory conceptual model of relationship initiation as a process of belief updating and theorize planning and early interaction as contexts in which potential signals of latent commitment may become observable. The concepts illuminate factors that may enable relationships to reach the level of mutual commitment needed to proceed or contribute to their premature termination. In practice, careful investment in selecting people with technical and relational attributes to send and interpret these signals is crucial when forming teams for complex collaborative projects.

title: Acquisitions among VC-backed entrepreneurial ventures: venture capitalists as information intermediaries
Why so few autonomous technology transfer offices? Organizational form choice in public research organizations in an emerging economy
abstract: Abstract Seven years after Brazil’s 2016 reform of the Innovation Law allowed public research organizations (PROs) to establish legally autonomous technology transfer offices (TTOs), uptake remained negligible. Drawing on administrative data obtained through freedom of information requests to Brazil’s Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, covering the 223 public PROs among the ministry’s 299 FORMICT respondents (public and private) for base year 2023, we find that fewer than 1% of public PROs have adopted the autonomous form; all 18 autonomous TTOs identified in public PROs are linked to just two organizations. Combining this baseline with document analysis of the innovation policies of eight reference PROs and interviews with domain experts and decision-makers about the broader institutional decision environment in which organizational-form choices occur, we examine why adoption diverges so sharply from the legal opportunity. The evidence is most consistent with the decision being shaped less by deliberate rejection than by an incremental decision architecture operating under limited information, short managerial horizons, and accountability pressures that favor defensible defaults. The findings extend the TTO literature by addressing the understudied question of how organizational form is chosen in emerging-economy PROs and offer policy implications for innovation-system governance.

title: How artificial intelligence changes technology transfer mechanisms: a systematic literature review
From social collaboration to algorithmic synthesis: the impact of GenAI on firms’ collaborative innovation
Mapping urban poverty: The unfolding of competing accounts through accounting visualizations
abstract: Poverty is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon whose definition and governance remain highly contested, despite its recognition as one of the most significant global challenges. While accounting plays a central role in constructing the poor and poverty through calculative practices, little is known about accounting visualizations creating a shared space for competing understandings of poverty to simultaneously unfold. We address this gap through a study of French urban policy documents. Our analysis focuses on the 2014 Lamy law, which introduced a new method for identifying poor urban areas eligible for public funding based primarily on mapped revenue data. Maps are particularly promising objects for such inquiry because, as the paper shows, they embed abstract accounting metrics into physical spaces and act as epistemic objects whose inherent incompleteness continuously stimulates further inquiry and knowledge development. Through this paper, we contribute to accounting research in two ways. First, we show that maps function as palimpsests of accounting information in which stable technical representations and successive partial accounts coexist within the same visual inscription, enabling the continuous exploration of complex epistemic objects. Second, we demonstrate that mapping accounting mediates the ‘distance-closeness’ tension in poverty governance by enabling local elected representatives to negotiate and develop alternative accounts of poverty despite enduring power asymmetries in favor of state representatives.

title: CEO overconfidence and the linguistic representation of corporate culture in 10-K filings: evidence from upper echelons theory
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether chief executive officer (CEO) overconfidence is associated with the linguistic representation of corporate culture in mandatory 10-K filings. Drawing on upper echelons theory, we argue that executives' psychological traits surface not only in strategic and financial outcomes but in the language through which corporate culture is communicated to external stakeholders, across the dimensions of control, collaboration, competition, and creation. Design/methodology/approach Using 27,742 firm-year observations from 2000 to 2022 drawn from Compustat, ExecuComp, and BoardEx, we measure CEO overconfidence through established option-exercise, stockholding, and investment proxies, and culture through textual analysis of 10-K filings. We estimate ordinary least squares models with year and industry fixed effects and assess robustness using firm fixed-effects models, lagged specifications, propensity score matching, entropy balancing, Heckman selection models, and instrumental variables. Findings CEO overconfidence is negatively associated with all four dimensions of culture-related language, with particularly pronounced associations for collective and procedural themes. The findings are robust across alternative specifications and identification strategies. The association is attenuated under female CEOs and more gender-diverse boards, concentrated in the discretionary Management Discussion and Analysis section, and accompanied by more optimistic and self-referential language, consistent with a managerial communication channel. Culture-related language is also associated with greater audit effort and market uncertainty and lower future performance. Supplementary pathway analysis reveals significant indirect associations for two overconfidence measures, linking the documented disclosure channel to economically relevant firm outcomes. Originality/value We extend upper echelons theory to the linguistic domain of regulated disclosure, showing that culture-specific language carries traces of managerial cognition even in collectively produced filings. By distinguishing control, collaboration, competition, and creation, the study also provides a practical framework through which auditors, boards, and reporting professionals can interpret culture-related language as a supplementary signal of managerial orientation, governance tone, and narrative-reporting risk.

title: The irrelevant responses and stock liquidity: dual validation evidence from the Chinese stock market using machine learning and large language models
abstract: Purpose As China’s capital market advances toward higher-quality development, the quality of corporate information disclosure and the transparency of managerial communication have become central concerns for investors and regulators. This study examines the relationship between managerial irrelevant responses during site visits and stock liquidity, and further investigates the underlying mechanisms through which such responses affect market liquidity. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Q&A records from site visits to A-share listed companies in China, this study constructs a quantitative measure of managerial irrelevant responses using machine learning techniques. In addition, online scoring based on a large language model (GPT-4) is introduced as a complementary indicator. Using regression analyses, we estimate the impact of irrelevant responses on stock liquidity and conduct mechanism and subgroup analyses to ensure robustness. Findings We find that managerial irrelevant responses are significantly negatively associated with stock liquidity. Mechanism analyses suggest that increased investor attention to financial issues reflects heightened uncertainty about firms’ future prospects, thereby exacerbating illiquidity. Furthermore, evasive or ambiguous managerial communication reduces analyst coverage, deteriorates the external information environment and further suppresses stock liquidity. Subgroup analyses reveal that this negative effect is more pronounced among firms without a price limit mechanism, firms with lower institutional ownership and firms receiving limited media attention. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature at the intersection of information disclosure and market microstructure by introducing a novel, text-based measure of managerial communication quality. The findings provide evidence on the real market consequences of evasive disclosure behavior and offer important policy implications for improving regulatory oversight and managerial communication practices in capital markets.

title: How Shared Values between Assurance Providers and Clients Can Impair Professional Skepticism: A Quasi-Experiment
Reviewing digital gaming and gambling addiction: A dark intersection of technology, psychology, and sociology
abstract: Digital gaming and digital gambling are converging into a single behavioural ecosystem in which loot boxes, social casino games, esports betting, and other hybrid mechanisms blur the historical boundary between gaming and gambling, generating addiction risks that no single discipline can fully explain. This study conducts a structured literature review of 78 studies focused on adults and emerging adults. The review first identifies recurring technological factors (gamification elements, immersive technologies, personalisation algorithms, and monetisation strategies) that act as triggers. These triggers activate psychological mechanisms (behavioural reinforcement, emotional regulation, impulse-control deficits, escapism, motivational drivers) and sociological mechanisms (cultural norms and peer influence, social connectivity and isolation, socio-demographic factors). Their interaction surfaces as recurring influence patterns that sustain problematic engagement. Building on these patterns, a conceptual framework is proposed that brings the triggers, mechanisms, and behavioural outcomes together as a coherent whole, connected through reinforcing feedback loops and a macro-design loop in which outcomes shape the next generation of triggers. The study advances theoretical understanding of digital addiction and equips designers and policymakers with a research agenda and intervention principles for mitigating harm without curbing legitimate digital entertainment.

title: The psychological cost of sharing: How personal information requirements affect e-government app adoption
abstract: E-government apps enable sustainable public governance, but their effectiveness hinges on citizens' willingness to use them. Drawing on self-determination theory, this research investigates how requirements for personal information sharing in e-government applications influence the intention to use the app. Four experiments conducted in Japan demonstrate that higher levels of required information sharing are negatively associated with citizens' intention to use an e-government app and to thereby help reduce the government's environmental footprint (more for consumers with overall environmental concerns, but less for consumers with specific concerns about government service sustainability). This negative association appears to be mediated by attitudes toward e-government app usability, the government, and the app's personal information management. When an e-government app is perceived as highly useful, mandatory information sharing triggers a positive attitude toward information management, counterbalancing the otherwise negative impact of mandatory personal information sharing. Gender moderates these relationships. Despite large within-gender variability, on average, women show greater sensitivity to privacy risks, stronger negative responses to mandatory information sharing, and a preference for diverse app functionalities, while men demonstrate a preference for streamlined, functionally similar services. The findings offer policymakers guidance on balancing the needs of sustainable governance with citizens' psychological well-being and privacy concerns.

title: Nine raters, one index: Carrying LLM disagreement into labour-market estimates
EXPRESS: Not All Are Created Equal: The Interplay Between Individual and Collective Agency in Collective Strategizing
abstract: Collective strategy has become increasingly important for bringing diverse actors together to address societal challenges, yet creating alignment between them remains difficult. As actors strategize collectively, they explore and experiment together, seeking to create alignment on a shared direction in what is initially a disordered situation. Drawing on a three-year process study of CareHub, an emerging collaboration developing an innovative neighbourhood-based healthcare service, we traced how actors navigate these tensions and how their individual and collective agency evolved dynamically as they did so. We identified six agentic moves, associated with either positional (granting mandate, relinquishing control, and constraining initiative) or peripheral (crafting emergent action, recovering bounded opportunities, and contesting authority) agency. Their intertwining shaped collective strategizing, despite the inequality in individual actors’ capacity to act. We extend the literature on collective strategizing by adopting a relational approach to show how different actors, including peripheral ones, mobilize agency and how their distinct forms of agency become intertwined in the process.

title: How to launch bug bounty programs: Strategies to utilize heterogeneous quality of hackers
Overcoming home institutional limitations via global platform involvement: A contingency perspective
abstract: Do institutional limitations inhibit or encourage entrepreneurship in the digital age? We advance research on this theoretical tension by focusing on global platform involvement, a novel strategic option. Specifically, we analyze how entrepreneurs access globally dispersed resources and escape certain limitations in home institutions. We argue that limitations in enabling institutions induce greater global platform involvement at the national level as a form of institutional escape, whereas limitations in constraining institutions persist as barriers to entrepreneurship and therefore deter such involvement. We further examine how formal and informal institutions interact to form configurations that jointly shape global platform involvement across countries. Based on these theoretical ideas, we propose a contingency-based perspective on the theoretical tension, emphasizing the type of focal institutions and their interactions. We test our hypotheses using data from a prominent global crowdfunding platform, where funding goals capture entrepreneurs’ intended engagement with the platform; our empirical analysis largely supports our arguments. We contribute to the international business literature by integrating contrasting viewpoints in the institution-based view and by extending the concept of institutional escapism to incorporate digital and entrepreneurial perspectives.

title: A Causal Inference Approach to Visitor Count at Open-Access Destinations
abstract: High visitor concentrations at open-access destinations create environmental and social challenges. Existing monitoring approaches can track visitor numbers but reveal little about factors that shape them. This paper applies causal inference theory to tourism research by showing how directed acyclic graphs can model and analyse visitor dynamics in outdoor destinations. Using two case studies from German leisure sites, it examines temporal, environmental and institutional influences on visitor count. Results show that daylight hours and weekends are the most stable predictors across both cases, while weather effects vary by destination context and activity profile. The study evaluates theory-driven hypotheses on the relative importance of temporal rhythms, environmental conditions and institutional calendars. Making assumed causal pathways explicit improves understanding the conditions associated with high visitor numbers, supports clearer research design and informs tailored management strategies. The study contributes to causal inference in tourism research and the sustainable management of open-access outdoor destinations.

title: What are social skills? Clarifying concepts, processes, and leadership effects
Climate transition risks and stock returns: Integrating multifactor models and machine learning
AI and Stress
abstract: ABSTRACT Given the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) tools at work, understanding their health implications is critically important. We use rich survey data from Finland and apply propensity score matching that accounts for observable differences between regular AI users and non‐users to estimate the relationship between reported AI usage at work and workers’ reported stress. Regular AI use is associated with a 4.4 percentage point higher probability of reporting stress, equivalent to a 25.6% increase relative to baseline. Comparing two competing explanations, we find that this pattern is more consistent with heavier work demands than with concerns about job loss: AI use is associated with more unpaid work outside working hours and, less precisely, with intense work absorption, but not with job insecurity. Exploratory subgroup estimates are larger and individually significant for men, non‐supervisors, unionized workers and employees in medium‐sized workplaces, although the differences across subgroups are not statistically significant.

title: Peer-country support for HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria programmes, Benin, Burkina Faso, Niger and Togo
abstract: Abstract Problem In the World Health Organization’s Regional Office for Africa, the previous inter-country technical support arrangements could not fully meet the growing and diverse needs of the 47 Member States. Approach The Regional Office therefore introduced multicountry assignment teams in 2022 to provide timelier, country-centred and integrated technical assistance. The multicountry assignment team for Benin, Burkina Faso, Niger and Togo organized comparative data analysis, thematic webinars, quarterly data reviews, peer-country visits and a best-practices workshop to strengthen the programme performance in human immunodeficiency virus, tuberculosis, malaria and hepatitis. Setting The four West African countries together have about 75 million people and have different programme performance levels. The countries also face different security constraints and service-delivery challenges. These factors create a strong rationale for structured peer learning and adaptation of proven practices. Relevant changes The initiative strengthened routine data use for decision-making, promoted peer support between countries and facilities, and contributed to practical service-delivery adaptations, including improved implementation of hepatitis B prevention of mother-to-child transmission after peer learning from Burkina Faso. Lessons learnt Structured peer-country support can accelerate programme improvement when it is anchored in routine data, focused on practical bottlenecks and translated into simplified, decentralized and task-shared service-delivery models.

title: The international legal framework for transporting infectious substances
abstract: Abstract Objective To examine international agreements, standards, policy documents and regulations governing the cross-border transportation of infectious substances and to assess the extent to which fragmented regulatory frameworks affect timely and safe shipment. Method A qualitative document analysis of 30 binding and non-binding legal and policy instruments was conducted and details were entered into a common extraction grid. In addition, the published reports and 64 international participants of World Health Organization (WHO) subregional workshops on the transport of infectious substances legislation, in Istanbul, Türkiye (2022) and Almaty, Kazakhstan (2023), provided an operational perspective. No other interviews or consultations were undertaken. Findings The analysis revealed substantial fragmentation and inconsistency in regulatory frameworks governing the cross-border transportation of infectious substances. Although many countries had ratified or referenced international agreements in national legislation, harmonized and cross-departmental implementation of legislation was lacking. Limitations included: (i) the incomplete adoption of international shipping standards; (ii) bureaucratic delays in approval and licensing processes; (iii) limited technical capacity; and (iv) a lack of standardized procedures and enforcement mechanisms. Conclusion The international regulatory environment for infectious substance transport is complex and targeted interventions are needed, such as harmonizing regulatory frameworks, improving interagency coordination, investing in capacity-building, developing standard operating procedures and aligning policy documents with international best practice. These interventions will help countries meet their obligations under the International Health Regulations (2005), enhance the safe and secure transport of infectious substances and improve global public health preparedness, as required by the recent WHO Pandemic Agreement.

title: When normal ends at the median: a design flaw in child growth charts, India
abstract: Abstract India's Integrated Child Development Services programme monitors the growth of approximately 63 million children through a network of 1.4 million community-based childcare centres called Anganwadi Centres. The weight-for-age growth charts currently used in the programme contain an important design flaw in how normal growth is represented. While they incorporate the World Health Organization (WHO) standard-deviation (SD) cut-offs to identify levels of undernutrition (−2 SD and −3 SD), the green band denoting normal growth is visually truncated at the median (0 SD), thus omitting the upper half of the WHO-defined normal range (i.e. between the median and +2 SD). Our analysis of weight-for-age data of 209 043 children surveyed in India's National Family Health Survey-5 showed that 24 888 children (11.9%) fell above the median and below +2 SD. This design flaw would place an estimated 7.5 million children outside the programme chart's current normal growth band, despite them falling within the WHO-defined normal range. Official training materials offer no clear guidance on interpreting the growth of children that plot in this range. The same truncated growth chart appears in the Mother and Child Protection Card, used widely in India’s health-care system. This paper documents the design flaw, examines its implications, quantifies the scale of impact and makes the case for corrective action. The timing for addressing the flaw is opportune: Indian decision-makers are developing growth references for India under the Upgrading Norms for Growth and Development Assessment of Indian Children initiative.

title: The WHO interim Medical Countermeasures Network for public health emergencies
abstract: Abstract Medical countermeasures, such as vaccines, diagnostics and therapeutics, are essential for effectively preparing for and responding to public health emergencies. The coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic and other emergencies, including the mpox and Ebola outbreaks, exposed deep-seated inequities and fragmentation in the global system for accessing and distributing medical countermeasures. In 2023, the World Health Organization (WHO) established the interim Medical Countermeasures Network following a call from Member States for a coordination mechanism to facilitate access to medical countermeasures in the event of another pandemic. The network’s aim is to enhance timely and equitable access to quality, safe, effective and affordable medical countermeasures during public health emergencies. Operating as an interim network of networks, the interim Medical Countermeasures Network brings together global and regional stakeholders across the medical countermeasures value chain, without pre-empting Member States’ prerogatives during deliberations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement. The network’s value was demonstrated in 2024 during the mpox public health emergency of international concern, when its structure was leveraged to operationalize an Access and Allocation Mechanism for limited vaccine supplies. Through coordinated partnerships, the mechanism enabled the strategic sourcing, allocation, transportation and distribution of 1.49 million mpox vaccine doses to beneficiaries in 15 countries. The experience offered valuable insights for preventing, preparing for and responding to future pandemics. The experience also highlighted the need for a sustainable, institutionalized mechanism to coordinate equitable access to medical countermeasure that is aligned with global instruments including the International health regulations (2005) and the WHO Pandemic Agreement, once it comes into force.

title: Health and economic impacts of China’s rural Toilet Revolution
abstract: Abstract Objective In 2015, China implemented the national Toilet Revolution, which aimed to upgrade toilets in rural areas. We quantified the health and economic impact of the Toilet Revolution from 2018 to 2024 by examining the association between sanitary toilet coverage and the incidence of diseases transmitted by the faecal–oral route. Method We used national and provincial data on sanitary toilet coverage and the reported incidence of faecal–oral diseases. We adjusted estimated associations by socioeconomic and environmental covariates. We calculated population-attributable fractions to estimate the preventable disease burden, and assessed economic benefits through reductions in treatment costs associated with a reduction in cases of faecal–oral diseases. Findings From 2018 to 2024, the estimated rural sanitary toilet coverage increased from an estimated 56% to 76%, while faecal–oral disease incidence declined substantially. A 1% increase in toilet coverage was associated with a 1.56% reduction in national incidence of disease. Overall, 16.87% (95% confidence intervals: 16.64 to 17.12) of the observed decline in the incidence of faecal–oral diseases was attributable to increased toilet coverage. This reduction corresponded to average annual treatment savings of 4.93 million yuan (¥; 1 United States dollar ≈ ¥ 6.80) and cumulative savings exceeding ¥ 200 million. Forward projections indicate that continued expansion of sanitary toilet coverage will further reduce disease incidence up to 2032. Conclusion Our analysis shows that provision of sanitation infrastructure is a high-impact population health intervention that produces sustained economic returns at scale.

title: Digital maturity and digital rehabilitation in prisons: organizational conditions for inclusion and reintegration
abstract: In an era of compulsory computing, incarceration produces acute forms of digital exclusion, limiting access to the technologies and skills increasingly required for participation in contemporary society. Digital rehabilitation has emerged as a response to this challenge by integrating digital access, skills development, and digital participation into correctional practice. However, the successful implementation of digital rehabilitation depends on both technology provision and broader organizational conditions. Drawing on Reisdorf and Rikard's (2018) Digital Rehabilitation Model and Knight et al.'s (2023) Digital Maturity framework, this paper examines how digital rehabilitation is implemented in highly digitally mature correctional systems and identifies the conditions that enable its development and sustainability. Using qualitative case studies from Southeast Asia, Western/Northern Europe, and Oceania, we analyze explicit digital rehabilitation interventions alongside the structural conditions that support them. Findings indicate that digital rehabilitation is most effective when supported by strategic leadership and governance, organizational capacity, collaborative partnerships and participation, and learning, evaluation, and adaptation. Although the three jurisdictions followed different pathways to digital transformation, all demonstrated strong alignment between rehabilitation goals and broader digital strategies. The findings also suggest that digitally mature prison systems are shaped by wider political and institutional environments, including national digital priorities, cross-sector coordination, and institutional capacity. We argue that digital maturity should be understood as an institutional capability that enables digital rehabilitation to become embedded within correctional practice. Where these conditions are present, digital rehabilitation has the potential to support digital inclusion, capability-building, reintegration, and broader public value outcomes.

title: Causal Machine Learning for Treatment Effect Heterogeneity: Interpretation, Benchmarking, Validation
abstract: Causal machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising approach for predicting individualized treatment effects and advancing precision medicine, moving beyond the limitations of conventional one-variable-at-a-time subgroup analyses of randomized trials. A recent benchmarking study by Chen and colleagues evaluated several causal ML learners across two large trials and concluded that current methods do not yet demonstrate reliable performance for clinical application. While such applied methodological investigations are valuable, this conclusion warrants a more nuanced examination. Multiple independent research groups have successfully applied causal ML across respiratory medicine and critical care, identifying clinically meaningful treatment effect heterogeneity that prior subgroup analyses had not resolved, although these applications have methodological limitations and do not yet establish that the detected heterogeneity is robust across internal and external validation. We outline four sequential and iterative dimensions central to credible causal ML analyses: choice of learner, model training with cross-fitting, internal validation using calibration-for-benefit and rank-weighted metrics, and external validation aligned with the original causal question. With careful methodological execution, causal ML holds considerable promise for personalized treatment decisions and warrants continued development; dismissing the field prematurely risks overlooking a powerful tool for personalized treatment decisions.

title: An encounter-based exposure measure for crash risk analysis: Model development and evidence from the Netherlands
Workload matters: A quantitative examination of caseload reform & job satisfaction in South African child protection
National comparative assessment of state outcome environments for youth transitions from foster care: Modeling the 2020 NYTD longitudinal cohort data set
Unplanned pregnancy and corporal punishment: Maternal depression as a mediator
abstract: Background Unplanned pregnancy, maternal depression, and corporal punishment are major public health concerns, yet their interplay remains poorly understood in low- and middle-income settings. Objective To examine whether maternal depression mediates the link between unplanned pregnancy and corporal punishment, and whether this indirect association is moderated by maternal education. Participants and setting Secondary analysis of 20,354 mothers from the nationally representative Peruvian ENDES surveys (2022–2024). Methods Structural equation modeling with complex survey design and multigroup analyses by education. Results Unplanned pregnancy was positively associated with depression (b = 0.198, p < .001), depression was associated with a greater likelihood of corporal punishment (b = 0.124, p < .001). The direct (b = 0.122) and indirect (b = 0.024) effects were significant ( p < .001). The standardized indirect effect was small (β = 0.012). Indirect paths differed by education: significant among secondary (b = 0.025) and higher (b = 0.031) groups, but not primary-or-less (b = 0.007; Wald χ 2 (2) = 10.14, p = .006). Conclusions Depression accounts for a small but detectable share of the association, yet due to the cross-sectional design and misaligned reference periods, results should be read as statistical associations, not causal evidence.

title: Addressing the challenge of saline-alkali soils through integration of soil microbiology, precision agriculture, and genomics for food security
The Dual Role of Social Media in LGBT Mental Health: Internalized Homophobia, Discrimination, and Connectedness
abstract: Abstract This study examined the association between internalized homophobia and mental health among LGBT individuals using a moderated multiple mediation model. Survey data from 478 Israeli sexual minority adults were analyzed to test whether community connectedness and perceived discrimination mediated this relationship, and whether overall and platform-specific social media use (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, and YouTube) moderated these pathways. Findings indicated that internalized homophobia was associated with poorer mental health both directly and indirectly through reduced connectedness and heightened discrimination. Community connectedness functioned as a protective factor, whereas discrimination was linked to poorer mental health. Social media use amplified the harmful indirect effect via discrimination while attenuating the protective pathway via connectedness, revealing its dual role in strengthening risk mechanisms and weakening resilience processes. These results extend minority stress theory into digital contexts by showing that social media can simultaneously intensify stress-related pathways and weaken protective mechanisms, underscoring the conditional nature of online engagement in shaping sexual minority people’s mental health.

title: Romantic Partner’s Body Odor and Relationship Quality
abstract: Abstract As a powerful medium for nonverbal social communication, body odors convey important cues about our romantic partner’s emotions. Since understanding each other’s emotions is crucial for romantic relationships, body odors may foster attachment and connection in these contexts. Using a survey study with 206 participants, we explored how the odor of a romantic partner influenced relationship quality. Specifically, we investigated whether individuals’ beliefs about their partner’s body odor were associated with explicit relationship quality indicators (relationship satisfaction, emotional and sexual intimacy) controlling for partner’s other traits. Our results showed the importance of thinking of a romantic partner’s odor as pleasant for sexual intimacy above and beyond other traits. We also provide preliminary evidence that the mere evaluation of a partner’s body odor was associated with feelings of safety and sexual arousal, which in turn predicted greater emotional and sexual intimacy, respectively. The present study advances our understanding of how body odors contribute to romantic chemistry and opens the way for more nuanced investigations.

title: Introduction to the Special Section on Artificial Intelligence and Sexuality
Exploring the Sexual Experiences of LGBTQ+ and Physically Disabled Individuals: Challenges, Accessibility, Pleasure, and Kink
From Reporting to Regulation: The Making and Governance of Financial Resilience Through the Charity Statement of Recommended Practice in England and Wales
abstract: This paper examines the emergence of the first charity accounting standard, the Statement of Recommended Practice 2: Accounting by Charities (SORP), to show how financial resilience came to be constructed within the sector. Moving beyond accounts which frame the SORP as a technical response to scandals of the 1980s, it situates its development within a longer trajectory of post-war welfare and regulatory reform. Drawing on Burchell et al.’s notion of arenas, the paper traces how the accounting profession helped connect concerns around poor financial reporting, fraud, financial mismanagement and weak regulatory oversight to the development of standardised reporting practices which made charities financially knowable, comparable and governable. By treating the SORP as a regulatory tool, the paper shows how accounting standards helped translated aspirations for stewardship into calculable and governable expectations of financial resilience.

title: From territorial deprivation trap to innovation precinct: A causal-asset framework for industrial heritage brownfield land use change
abstract: Preservation-led programs dominate the regeneration of heritage-industrial brownfields in Global South cities, overshadowing territorial assets, constraints, and demand. Few replicable, demand-first, multi-scale frameworks explain how post-industrial land-use changes can be derived in institutionally complex and economically stressed contexts. This research proposes a causal-asset framework based on sustainable urban livelihoods, asset-based community development, and system dynamics to study the role of assets, barriers, and feedback loops in determining adaptive reuse strategies. The framework is applied to the Ray Cement Factory, Tehran, Iran, a case rich in information combining national industrial heritage, long-term underuse, metropolitan accessibility, university assets, and reuse constraints. The methodology innovatively integrated three-scale asset inventory; purposive group model building; causal diagramming; and strategy derivation. The analysis reveals two interconnected negative dynamics due to the absence of innovative spatial infrastructure. One is a territorial deprivation trap characterized by skills deficits and suppressed entrepreneurship, and the other is an asset underutilization trap that leads to heritage deterioration and disinvestment. The breaking of this link can trigger two self-reinforcing structures, the Innovation Ecosystem Loop and the Heritage Identity Loop, that underpin precinct viability. This study contributes by deriving programming from diagnosed territorial demand. It operationalizes heritage-historical capital as a non-substitutable, stock-like category grounded in a national-first industrial identity. The findings indicate that asset-strategy coherence requires alignment at the metropolitan, immediate urban, and site levels. The framework helps planners connect heritage protection, economic activation, and policy coordination.

title: Geopolitical sequencing in Europe's energy transition: infrastructure, legitimacy and finance

Asymmetric active sites in rare-earth orthoferrites: Structural origins, dynamic evolution, and selective photocatalysis
Assessing energy justice in low-carbon transitions: Can system dynamics modeling contribute?
abstract: The growing awareness of asymmetries in low-carbon transitions has intensified efforts to integrate energy justice into quantitative assessment tools. However, guidance remains limited on how to incorporate justice considerations into modeling processes while preserving their normative and context-dependent character. This study proposes a conceptual-methodological meta-framework for systematically relating energy justice to system dynamics (SD) modeling. Rather than prescribing an operational modeling framework, the meta-framework provides structured guidance on how justice concerns and tenets, spatial and temporal scales, and stakeholder perspectives can and should inform problem framing, operationalization, model development, and interpretation. This paper examines the meta-framework's usefulness through a retrospective and reflexive analysis of research activities on Portugal's electric vehicle (EV) transition conducted between 2021 and 2025. The analysis illustrates how justice considerations shape model boundaries, indicator selection, causal structures, and the interpretation of model outputs, while simultaneously exposing key limitations in operationalization and normative assumptions. The contributions and limitations of SD modeling for this type of assessment are also discussed. Particularly, SD should not be used as a standalone tool for justice assessment, but as one component of a broader, methodologically plural approach. Overall, this work provides conceptual and methodological guidance for more explicit and reflexive integration of energy justice into quantitative assessments of low-carbon transitions.

title: Comparing mineral resource potential and theoretical economic value in desalination brines and oilfield produced waters: a screening-level assessment
Toward protein quality-matched transitions and their climate mitigation potential across Europe
Rapid Emission–Economy Decoupling alongside the Urbanization of Chinese Counties
abstract: Abstract As China makes progress in air pollution control, the growing need for targeted pollution mitigation poses a great challenge for fine-scale emission tracking. However, the lack of up-to-date high-resolution emission data precludes a timely, spatially detailed assessment of emission distributions and their evolution with economic development. Here we derive summertime nitrogen oxides emissions from 2018 to 2024 for a total of 2,842 counties at different levels of urbanization in mainland China, based on satellite measurements and a fast, physics-based emission inversion method. The results show widespread declines in 84.1 ± 7.3% of counties. Among the 1,779 counties with available gross domestic product data, 76.7 ± 7.1% achieve absolute emission-economy decoupling (i.e., reduced emissions despite economic growth), and an additional 9.4 ± 3.9% exhibit relative decoupling (i.e., economic growth outpacing emissions growth). Relative emission reductions and emission-economy decoupling tend to be stronger in more urbanized counties, with the share of total national emissions moving toward less-urbanized, previously less-focused counties, particularly in the west. These results suggest structural progress toward greener development in Chinese counties along with an emerging need to shift attention toward less-urbanized locations.

title: Ultrafast NH4+ Capture by Prussian Blue Analogues Accelerated by the Hydrogen-Bond of Water
abstract: Abstract Recovering ammonium (NH4+) from low-concentration wastewater represents a critical step toward sustainable nitrogen management. Although adsorption is widely regarded as the most promising strategy for NH4+ recovery from dilute streams, its practical application is often hampered by intrinsically slow kinetics and insufficient selectivity. Given the exceptional ion-sieving capability of Prussian blue analogues (PBAs), we hypothesized that water molecules confined within their framework channels create a dynamic hydrogen-bonded microenvironment that can modulate NH4+ transport. Inspired by this concept, we synthesized a series of Zn-based PBAs with controlled water contents via thermal treatment (denoted as Zn-PBAs-x, where x represents the treatment temperature). The sample with the highest water content (Zn-PBAs-60) exhibited an unprecedented NH4+ adsorption rate, with a pseudo-second-order rate constant (k2) of 4.35 g·mg–1·min–1. Integrated solid-state 1H magic-angle-spinning nuclear magnetic resonance (1H MAS NMR) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed a “water-accelerated adsorption” mechanism: hydrogen-bonding interactions between framework nitrogen sites and water molecules significantly weaken the binding of NH4+ to the framework, thereby markedly accelerating NH4+ migration within the channels. This material achieved nearly 20-fold concentration of dilute NH4Cl within 3 min. This study provides new insights and strategic directions for the rapid enrichment and resource utilization of low-concentration ammonia nitrogen, contributing to the advancement of sustainable development pathways.

title: Integrated Network Toxicology and Multi-Level Validations Unravel the Potential Mechanism Linking Phthalate Ester Exposure and Endocrine Diseases
abstract: Abstract Phthalate esters (PAEs) are endocrine-disrupting chemicals that can imitate endogenous hormones to disrupt the endocrine system. However, the upstream molecular initiating events (MIEs) by which PAEs trigger endocrine diseases, especially their interactions with receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), remain poorly understood. Here, we discovered that the targets of low molecular weight (LMW) and high molecular weight (HMW) PAEs highly overlapped with breast cancer-related targets, with an even greater overlap for HMW PAEs. Mechanistically, PAEs promoted breast cancer progression by activating the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mediated signaling pathway, with EGFR identified as a key kinase. Molecular interaction analysis confirmed that PAEs directly bind to EGFR, inducing its dimerization, with the benzene ring, ketone, methyl, and ether groups of PAEs being crucial. Notably, HMW PAEs exhibited stronger dimerization effects. This PAE-induced EGFR dimerization was determined to be the MIE in PAE-induced breast cancer. Furthermore, PAEs increased EGFR expression (2.44-fold), subsequently activating the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway, which promoted breast cancer cell proliferation to 165.34% and tumor growth to 229.05% of the control, with HMW PAEs again having stronger effects. This study identifies a previously unrecognized MIE–PAE-induced EGFR dimerization, linking PAE exposure to RTK–driven breast cancer and offering potential targets for prevention and intervention in breast cancer.

title: Decoupling Ion Selectivity and Transport via Dual-Scale Interlayer Nanochannels in Reduced Graphene Oxide Membranes for Lithium Separation
abstract: Abstract Selective separation of Li+ from coexisting Ni2+, Co2+, and Mn2+ is an important step in lithium recovery from spent lithium-ion batteries. Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) membranes offer a promising platform for this separation through their ångström-scale interlayer nanochannels. However, the same narrow nanochannels hinder ion diffusion, inducing a severe permeability–selectivity trade-off. To decouple ion selectivity from transport, we report a nanoconfined sol–gel strategy for constructing a dual-scale interlayer architecture in rGO membranes. Intercalated between graphene oxide layers, aluminosilicate (AS) sols serve as cross-linkers and in situ vapor sources. During thermal aging, sol–gel condensation generates vapor that expands un-cross-linked galleries into transport highways, while cross-linked domains retain ion-selective confinement. The architecture is tunable across ion-selective interlayer spacing (dS, 7.1–8.3 Å) and expanded interlayer spacing (dE, 34–94 Å). Compared with conventional rGO membranes, the optimized dual-scale spacing membrane increases Li+ permeability 5.4-fold in mixed-ion solution while achieving high divalent-ion selectivity (Li+/Ni2+ = 246, Li+/Co2+ = 391, Li+/Mn2+ = 448). Molecular dynamics simulations attribute this selectivity to asymmetric energy barriers imposed on Li+ and divalent cations within the cross-linked spacing, while the expanded spacing facilitates low-resistance transport. This work shows how nanoconfined sol–gel chemistry can open a design space for fabricating high-performance ion recovery membranes.

title: Identification and Reaction Analysis of Antibiotic Transformation Products in an Urban River via Suspect and Nontarget Screening with a Self-Curated Library
abstract: Abstract Antibiotics enter urban river basins mainly through sewage effluent. They undergo transformation during treatment and in river systems, generating transformation products (TPs) that may still have ecological effects. Yet, identifying these TPs by high-resolution mass spectrometry is hindered by the scarcity of reference standards and comprehensive MS/MS spectral libraries. To overcome this, we constructed a dedicated MS/MS library containing over 6,500 MS/MS spectra for 244 parent antibiotics and 362 TPs, thereby enabling rapid suspect screening through spectral matching. For novel TPs beyond library coverage, we integrated diagnostic fragment searching and seed-driven molecular networking to propagate annotations to structurally related unknowns. Applying this workflow to water, sediment, and effluent samples from an urban river system in Beijing, we identified 39 parent antibiotics and 158 TPs, of which 20 TPs are not previously documented in environmental samples. The major transformation reactions were cleavage, dealkylation, and hydrolysis, alongside compound-specific pathways like hemiacetal formation for erythromycin. These reactions differentially affect the environmental properties of antibiotics, and some reactions (e.g., dehydrogenation and dehydration) showed potential to enhance ecotoxicity. These results confirm that transformation substantially diversifies antibiotic signatures in urban aquatic environments and underscore the necessity of including TPs in environmental monitoring and risk assessment.

title: Dissolved Organic Matter Charge Dynamics over Three Decades
abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is a crucial component of aquatic ecosystems, influencing pH, metal speciation, and the bioavailability of trace elements. The influence of DOM on water quality depends not only on its concentration but also on its chemical characteristics. To quantify the site density (SD) of organic acid functional groups, a key characteristic of DOM, this study utilized data from over 31,000 water samples collected from 110 watercourses between 1995 and 2024 by Swedish national monitoring programs. We found systematic dynamic trends in SD across Sweden. The analysis revealed an increase in SD from 1995 to 2003, followed by a decline from 2003 to 2010. Since 2010, SD has stabilized, although modest increases remain evident at many sites. Earlier trends were potentially governed by changes in DOM mobility associated with recovery from acid deposition, whereas more recent trends are likely linked to DOM source characteristics.

title: Function of Submerged Macrophytes in the Distribution of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Alternatives in Constructed Wetlands: Role of Extracellular Polymeric Substances (EPS) in the Phyllosphere
abstract: Abstract Submerged macrophytes in constructed wetlands (CWs) are key to removing PFAS alternatives, which pose serious risks to aquatic ecosystems. Although phyllosphere extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) are crucial for contaminant uptake by submerged macrophytes, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that typical PFAS alternatives, 6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonate (F-53B) and hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (GenX), accumulated in Vallisneria spinulosa (V. spinulosa) reached 17.49 ± 1.02 and 5.25 ± 0.36 μg/g DW, respectively, approximately 2.70 and 3.16-fold higher than those in Ceratophyllum demersum (C. demersum). Correspondingly, the phyllosphere EPS of V. spinulosa exhibited high accumulation of GenX and F-53B, with concentrations of 124.98 ± 4.70 and 99.53 ± 13.12 μg/g DW, respectively. Crucially, EPS binding with PFAS alternatives increased the hydrophilicity and induced structural reorganization, facilitating contaminant internalization into plant tissues. Meanwhile, metagenomic analysis revealed that the phyllosphere microenvironment selectively enriched microbial functional genes involved in antioxidant defense and EPS biosynthesis, thus supporting sustained contaminant capture in the phyllosphere interface. These findings reveal EPS-mediated mechanisms underlying PFAS alternative uptake by submerged macrophytes in CWs.

title: Plankton Size Structure Impacts PAH Bioaccumulation and Fate in Marine Pelagic Food Webs
abstract: Abstract Plankton constitutes the primary entry point of contaminants into pelagic food webs, yet the role of plankton size structure in governing hydrocarbon fate remains poorly understood due to methodological limitations. Here, polycyclic aromatic (PAHs) and aliphatic (AHs) hydrocarbons were investigated across seven plankton size fractions (0.7 μm to >500 μm) collected in coastal waters of the northwestern Mediterranean Sea using a locally designed online sequential filtration system. Biochemical, isotopic, and molecular marker analyses were combined to characterize plankton composition, hydrocarbon sources, and PAH bioaccumulation patterns across size fractions. Molecular markers confirmed the transition from phytoplankton-dominated signatures in the smallest fractions to increasing zooplanktonic contributions in larger fractions. The 0.7–2.7 and 2.7–20 μm fractions, dominated by pico- and nanoplankton, accounted for the highest particulate organic carbon and hydrocarbon concentrations (3.0–3.4 μg g–1 dw for Σ26-PAHs) while zooplankton fractions (>60 μm) displayed lower values (0.09–0.69 μg g–1 dw). The passive uptake of low-molecular-weight (LMW) PAHs dominated across all size fractions but decreased with increasing plankton size. In contrast, high-molecular-weight (HMW) PAHs showed preferential accumulation in nanoplankton. These results demonstrate that plankton size structure and biomass dependent processes strongly influence PAH bioaccumulation and trophic transfer in marine pelagic food webs.

title: Microplastics Promote Light-Driven Ferrihydrite Transformation by Altering the Balance between Interfacial Aggregation and Redox Processes
abstract: Abstract Ferrihydrite (Fh) phototransformation regulates iron cycling and the mobility of nutrients and contaminants in aquatic and terrestrial environments. Microplastics (MPs) increasingly coexist with Fh, yet whether intact MP particles regulate Fh phototransformation through particle-scale interfacial effects remains unclear. We investigated how MPs (polystyrene (PS), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polylactic acid (PLA)) affect Fh transformation under simulated solar irradiation. Without MPs, irradiation produced predominantly hematite (Hm), with goethite (Gt) as a minor product, and 9.17% of Fh was transformed after 25 d. MPs increased the transformation without changing detectable products. MPs suppressed Fh reaggregation by shifting surface charge and disrupting Fh–Fh contacts, while enhancing irradiation-induced charge separation, surface Fe(III) reduction, Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling, and Fe mobilization. The promoting effects outweighed aggregation inhibition, causing net promotion of Fh transformation. Notably, PLA hydrolysis and photo-oxidation lowered pH and released acidic, Fe-complexing photoproducts, amplifying Fe mobilization and the aqueous Fe pathway. Overall, the PLA > PVC > PS trend reflects coupled polymer chemistry, particle properties, intact-particle interactions, and irradiation susceptibility, with PLA-derived aqueous components providing an additional solution-phase contribution. These findings show that intact MPs and polymer-derived aqueous products jointly modify Fe mineral evolution, linking plastic aging to iron biogeochemistry in illuminated surface environments.

title: Paleoclimatic Legacies Help Explain Microbial Carbon Use Efficiency in Thawing Permafrost
abstract: Abstract Microbial decomposition in thawing permafrost mobilizes one of Earth’s largest organic carbon reservoirs, releasing CO2 that amplifies global warming. This carbon–climate feedback depends strongly on microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE)─the ratio of biomass carbon synthesis to total carbon uptake, which governs the balance between carbon retention and respiratory loss. Although permafrost carbon and microbial communities developed thousands of years ago, how paleoclimatic legacies shape permafrost CUE remains unresolved. Here, by integrating 18O–H2O labeling with amplicon and metagenomic sequencing across a ∼1000-km transect on the Tibetan Plateau, we show that mid-Holocene paleoclimate outperforms contemporary drivers in explaining spatial variation in permafrost CUE. Sites with drier and more variable paleoclimates exhibited lower CUE (0.17 ± 0.07) than wetter and more climatically stable sites (0.43 ± 0.08). This lower CUE was linked to two pathways: geochemical constraints involving reduced nutrient availability and stronger phosphorus limitation, and microbial adaptations reflected in communities enriched in metabolically costly stress-tolerance and recalcitrant carbon-acquisition traits. Collectively, these paleoclimatic legacies accounted for 70% of CUE variation, underscoring the critical role of paleoclimate in shaping the vulnerability of permafrost carbon to respiratory loss upon thawing. Incorporating these millennial-scale legacies into Earth system models could improve projections of future permafrost carbon feedbacks.

title: A Substitution Paradox in China’s Plastics Sector: Climate Benefits of Degradable Materials Are Conditional on Energy-System Decarbonization
abstract: Abstract Plastics are a rapidly growing source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Degradable plastics are increasingly promoted to address plastic waste concerns, while biobased alternatives are also considered for their potential to reduce reliance on fossil feedstocks and lower life cycle GHG emissions. However, their system-level climate effects remain uncertain because existing assessments often focus on individual products or polymers and rarely account for realistic substitution feasibility, value-chain interactions, and end-of-life (EoL) constraints. Here, we integrated dynamic material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, and scenario modeling to evaluate the net GHG implications of substituting degradable plastics across China’s plastics sector. The framework tracks five major conventional resins across 14 application sectors, links sector-specific substitution pathways with production-stage carbon intensities, and quantifies emission trajectories from 2025 to 2030, with long-term mitigation pathways explored to 2060. Technically feasible substitution increases cumulative life cycle GHG emissions by 7.1% relative to the conventional baseline because higher upstream production emissions outweigh potential EoL credits for recovered energy or displaced coproducts. Scenario analysis identifies a critical transition threshold: degradable plastics achieve net GHG reductions only when energy-system carbon intensity decreases by approximately 47% of the baseline level. The climate benefits of substitution are therefore conditional on coordinated energy-system decarbonization, production improvement, and waste-management development. Even under the optimistic pathway, 0.24 Gt CO2e of residual emissions remain in 2060, indicating the need for complementary mitigation measures.

Artificial intelligence in life cycle assessment: methods, applications and challenges
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping how Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is applied in sustainability research and industry practice. This review aims to examine how AI is being applied across the stages of LCA, focusing on its applications, capabilities and key challenges, and on its role as a complement to established LCA methods. Eligible studies were identified through a systematic search covering 2010–2026, using conventional AI and machine-learning terms together with extended terms for large language models (LLMs), generative AI and AI agents. Evidence from 39 eligible studies, all published between 2021 and 2026 and reflecting the recent emergence of AI-enabled LCA research, was synthesised, with twelve studies selected for further detailed comparative analysis based on (i) diversity of the AI methodological approaches used and (ii) their contributions to LCA data quality, modelling capability, and interpretability. Foundational AI and LCA methodology literature was incorporated through backward citation tracking to provide context. Half of the twelve studies selected for detailed comparison applied or reviewed machine-learning or neuro-fuzzy models, including two reviews that synthesise a wider body of ML applications (e.g., 81 studies in Ghoroghi et al., 2022). These studies mainly reported gains in predictive accuracy, which depended on the quality of the training data and on validation, while uncertainty and incomplete inventory data remained recurring limitations. At the same time, ontology-based and digital-twin frameworks can offer greater data interoperability and support dynamic assessment. LLM- and agent-based approaches are emerging as a means of automating data retrieval and wider LCA workflows but remain at an early stage of validation. Persistent challenges include opaque model logic, high computational demand, inconsistent data governance, and limited ethical oversight. Addressing these issues will require transparent modelling protocols, energy-aware computation, and harmonised data standards supported by cross-sector governance. Unlike previous reviews that focus predominantly on machine learning applications, this review provides a comparative synthesis of machine learning, LLM, ontology-based, digital-twin, and agent-based approaches across the full LCA workflow. Our analysis of reviewed literature indicates that AI has significant potential to enhance LCA efficiency, data interoperability, and decision support, while highlighting the need for greater transparency, rigorous validation, and robust governance frameworks to support wider adoption. The review advances the field by proposing a conceptual framework for evaluating the strengths, limitations, scalability, and interpretability of AI applications in LCA, together with practical recommendations for developing accountable, energy-efficient, and policy-relevant sustainability analytics.

title: Nitrogen and Phosphorus Losses in a Rural Watershed Under no Tillage System in Southern Brazil
abstract: ABSTRACT Intensive production is sought by farmers but may compromise sustainability depending on management. No‐Tillage System (NTS) is a conservation system and paradigm in Brazilian grain production; however, the quality of its adoption is questioned as water erosion regained importance and remains underestimated. This study quantified nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) concentrations and losses and evaluated the seasonal contribution of soluble and particulate fractions to nutrient export in a rural watershed under long‐term NTS without terraces in southern Brazil. A 118.8‐ha watershed comprising 13 agricultural fields was monitored from December 2022 to November 2023. Streamflow was continuously monitored at the watershed outlet, while daily streamwater samples were collected and analyzed for total, soluble, and particulate N and P. Nitrate (N‐NO 3 − ) and ammonium (N‐NH 4 + ) concentrations remained below the Brazilian critical environmental limit (CEL), whereas TP frequently exceeded the 0.10 mg L −1 threshold. Particulate N (PN) accounted for 70.20% of total N (TN) export, while particulate P (PP) accounted for 97.65% of total P (TP) export, demonstrating the predominance of particulate pathways. Nutrient losses increased markedly during intense precipitation and high streamflow, particularly in October and November. Annual losses reached 30.80 kg N ha −1 and 4.91 kg P ha −1 , corresponding to monetary losses of US$ 22.58 ha −1 and US$ 4.85 ha −1 , respectively. Overall, long‐term NTS alone was insufficient to prevent substantial nutrient losses under high‐flow conditions, particularly in particulate form. Integrating NTS with mechanical runoff control practices and effective soil cover is therefore essential to improve soil and water conservation in agricultural watersheds.

title: Geographic Integration and Firm Exports: Evidence from China,
abstract: Abstract Domestic connectivity via passenger transport infrastructure can affect a country’s exports by easing information frictions. We study this mechanism using China’s high-speed rail network, which connects cities to same-sector exporters in other cities without directly affecting freight costs. Stronger connections increase firms’ export sales and expand both destination and product scope, with no change in domestic sales, total employment, or shipping costs. The effects are largest for firms facing greater information barriers. Connected firms upgrade product quality and their export destinations converge toward those of newly connected peers, with initially weaker firms converging toward stronger connected peers while stronger firms show little adjustment. A within-firm cross-destination specification confirms that improved connectivity generates destination-specific benefits. The results point to an information-based channel through which passenger connectivity affects trade, including knowledge about export markets and inputs.
journal_name: Journal of the European Economic Association

title: Rigorous Engaged Scholarship
abstract: Abstract Scholars are increasingly asked to address societal grand challenges. Yet forms of scholarship that pursue these aims through engagement with practice are often treated with suspicion. In this Point, we intend to zoom in on this paradox. We argue that engaged scholarship requires rethinking what it means to be rigorous when working closely with practitioners. We advance this conversation by defining a novel set of six principles to guide its rigor: articulating positionality, orienting prospectively, collaborating critically, experimenting systematically, appearing visibly, and reflecting inwardly. These principles enhance current norms in management studies regarding knowledge production, leading us to suggest how the institutional environment will need to change to support rigorous engaged scholarship.

title: Exploring the Dark Side of the Coopetition Paradox: Unintentional Knowledge Leakage, Capital Structure, and Organizational Decline in Small‐Firm Coopetition
abstract: Abstract While paradox theory's generative view implicitly assumes that actors possess the agency to navigate contradictory pursuits productively, an emerging dark‐side perspective suggests that power relations and material constraints may transform such pursuits into pragmatic paradoxes. Building on this perspective, we explore how constrained paradox navigation manifests in behavioural dysfunction and contributes to organizational decline. We study this process in small‐firm coopetition, where boundary‐spanning managers experience the paradoxical tension of coopetition while juggling persistent, contradictory demands. We propose that this tension is positively associated with unintentional knowledge leakage (UKL), a boundary‐regulation failure whereby managers inadvertently disclose sensitive knowledge to a competing partner. In turn, UKL relates to organizational decline, thereby mediating the tension–decline relationship, while capital structure (financial leverage) amplifies the tension–UKL association. Using survey and archival data from 236 Swedish small technology‐manufacturing firms, we find support for these relationships. We advance paradox theory by identifying boundary‐regulation failure as a distinct dark‐side dysfunction and financial leverage as a material boundary condition that exacerbates the constraining effects of paradox navigation. We also reorient coopetition research from intentional partner appropriation toward inadvertent disclosure by the focal firm's own managers. Practically, we highlight the importance of financial resilience in preserving managers' discretion when navigating coopetition's dark side.

title: Multispecies Care and Emotional Life at Work: Organizational Cynicism, Work Alienation, and the Moderating Role of the Work–Pet Family Interface
Can Europe afford to phase out Russian gas? How timing, global supply conditions, and demand shape wholesale gas prices
Mapping Aluminum Flows in the United States Using Advanced Bayesian Material Flow Analysis
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a Bayesian material flow analysis (MFA) of aluminum in the U.S. economy, reconciling a 2017 baseline and updating the system through 2022. We introduce ARCADE (Abiotic Resource Cycles, Allocations, and Dynamics in the Economy), a unified Bayesian MFA framework integrating system definition, data pedigree, and probabilistic reconciliation under physical constraints. ARCADE combines government statistics, trade records, and industry reports into a physically consistent network and reports uncertainty-aware metrics. Results show continued U.S. reliance on imports of unwrought and finished aluminum products. The posterior median end-of-life (EOL) collection rate was 66.8% [57.2%, 79.9%] in 2017 and 67.6% [62.3%, 73.9%] in 2022. Median domestic retention of collected EOL scrap was lower in 2022 (52.7% [49.6%, 55.6%]) than in 2017 (56.4% [51.7%, 60.5%]), although the credible interval for the change spanned zero. Across robustness cases varying source weighting, pedigree-to-uncertainty mappings, and prior strength, domestic retention remained below 60%. Spatial analysis identified mismatches between EOL scrap generation and domestic remelting capacity. These findings show that improved collection alone may not increase domestic recycling when processing constraints persist. We observe a continued import dependence, efficient circulation of prompt fabrication scrap, and limited domestic retention of collected EOL scrap.

title: Unresolved Complex Mixture of Hydrocarbons as a Potential Stratigraphic Anthropogenic Marker for the Great Acceleration
abstract: Abstract The unresolved complex mixture (UCM) consists of chromatographically unresolvable branched, cyclic, and aromatic hydrocarbons, which are intermediate- to semivolatile organic compounds primarily derived from anthropogenic fossil fuel usage, including industrial emissions and gasoline and diesel exhaust. The UCM in natural archives, expressed as its ratio to resolved compounds (UCM/R), may thus provide an indication of fossil fuel-derived contamination in the environment over time. To test this hypothesis, accurately dated sediment records from the Black Sea, the Baltic Sea, and the northeastern Germany Tiefer See lake were analyzed for hydrocarbons. Each record presents a similar temporal pattern with a synchronous main increase of UCM/R in the early 1950s and a decrease in the 1990s. This UCM/R pattern most likely reflects the pronounced increase in the use of petroleum-derived products during the Great Acceleration of the mid-20th century and, subsequently, the application of filters and catalytic converters to reduce volatile organic compound emissions in the 1980s–1990s. Therefore, UCM/R in recent sediments represents a stratigraphic anthropogenic marker for the Great Acceleration in European midlatitudes and, if replicated globally, could be a further marker for the beginning of the Anthropocene as a potential geological epoch.

title: The hinge of the golden door: Labor market impacts of immigrant exclusion

The French touch: Product quality and France's great trade liberalization, 1850–74
abstract: Abstract We explore changes in product quality during France's major liberalization episode of the mid‐nineteenth century. Using new data and existing techniques from the international trade literature, we investigate the relative quality of French products versus those of international competitors, within‐industry changes in quality, and within‐product quality changes. France produced relatively high‐quality, high unit value products in the traded sector throughout the period. Liberalization was associated with an overall decline in the quality of French exports. However, some of the best‐selling exports experienced an apparent rise in quality around the time of liberalization. As for imports, whilst French spending may have switched to lower‐quality products due to liberalization, lower tariffs were associated with rising within‐product quality.

Drought Impacts and Recovery Across Agricultural Regions: Evidence on Farm Economic Returns to Labour From a Synthetic Control Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the economic impacts of drought remains challenging, particularly in identifying causal effects and accounting for regional heterogeneity. This paper applies the Synthetic Control Method (SCM) to estimate the impact of the 2017–2020 drought on economic returns to agricultural labour across three main agricultural regions in New South Wales, Australia. Using a 30‐year panel from the ABARES Australian Agricultural and Grazing Industries Survey, we construct counterfactual trajectories for total cash receipts per unit of labour to assess how outcomes would have evolved in the absence of drought. The results reveal substantial spatial heterogeneity in both the magnitude and persistence of impacts: the North West region experienced a decline of approximately 57% but recovered by 2022, the Central West shows persistent losses relative to its counterfactual by 2022, and the Riverina exhibits only limited deviations, suggesting greater resilience. These findings highlight that drought impacts differ not only in severity but also in recovery dynamics across regions and demonstrate the value of SCM as a transparent and replicable approach for estimating regional economic impacts using publicly available data, with important implications for place‐based drought policy.

title: On the economic benefit of subset regression for the multivariate HAR model
abstract: Forecasts of the covariance matrix of returns is a crucial input into portfolio construction. In recent years, multivariate versions of the Heterogenous AutoRegressive (HAR) models have been designed to utilize realized measures of the covariance matrix to generate forecasts, including in the context of direct forecasts of the portfolio weights. This paper shows that combination forecasts using a subset regression approach provide more stable coefficient estimates and, as a result, more stable forecasts and lower portfolio turnover. The economic benefits of this approach become crucial when transaction costs are taken into account. The direct methods outperform indirect methods, consistent with the previous literature, and smaller models and their combinations are the best-performing overall. These benefits are observed for a range of covariance matrix estimators and portfolio dimensions. Economic benefits are observed at 1-day, 1-week, and 1-month ahead forecast horizons and corresponding portfolio holding periods.
