Stakeholder perspectives on incentives and misalignments in prospective sustainable ship recycling: The Finnish maritime cluster
abstract: Ship recycling can recover substantial material and component value from end-of-life vessels, but responsible dismantling also requires strict environmental, safety, and waste management standards. These requirements may improve sustainability performance while increasing the costs and risks borne by the actors responsible for end-of-life decisions. Previous research has identified major economic, environmental, regulatory, technological, and organizational barriers to sustainable ship recycling, as well as stakeholder conflicts and incentive problems. However, limited empirical attention has been given to how value and burdens are perceived to be distributed across actors, where these distributions become misaligned, and how respondents associate possible responses with such misalignments in prospective high-standard recycling systems. This study examines these issues in the context of the prospective development of domestic sustainable ship recycling in Finland, drawing on 50 open-ended questionnaire responses from maritime actors and experts. The responses were analyzed through thematic analysis. The analysis indicates that respondents perceived potential value across material recovery, business opportunities, environmental and social outcomes, and knowledge development, whereas key costs, risks, and responsibilities were located at specific decision and investment points. Four recurring forms of perceived misalignment were identified: end-of-life decision misalignment, standards-cost misalignment, lifecycle misalignment, and flow-investment misalignment. The analysis links respondents' proposed responses to these four interpretive categories, although their feasibility and effectiveness were not tested. The study offers a differentiated, context-specific framework for understanding stakeholder perspectives on the prospective viability of high-standard ship recycling in Finland and provides implications for the future development of sustainable ship-recycling capacity in Finland and comparable maritime settings.

title: Environmental sustainability begins at the top: The combined role of CEO attention and power

Attributional and consequential life cycle assessment of end-of-life options for flexible pipelines from oil well decommissioning
abstract: Decommissioning oil wells in Brazil will generate large quantities of subsea pipelines that require end-of-life (EoL) management. This study evaluated four EoL options for flexible pipelines using attributional and consequential life cycle assessment (LCA) with system expansion: (1) landfill disposal; (2) steel recycling combined with mechanical recycling of high-density polyethylene (HDPE), polyamide (PA), and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF); (3) steel recycling combined with energy recovery from HDPE and PA and mechanical recycling of PVDF; and (4) pipeline reuse. Substitution rates of 100% for recycled polymers and 24% for steel scrap were adopted, and their effects were evaluated through sensitivity analyses. For reuse, the difference between well and pipeline service lives resulted in a Reuse Efficiency Factor (REF) of 37.5%, which was used to calculate the credit for avoided new pipeline manufacturing. Attributional LCA identified landfill disposal as the lowest-impact option, whereas, under the adopted substitution and reuse assumptions, consequential LCA produced the opposite ranking, with reuse showing the lowest impacts, generally followed by mechanical recycling, energy recovery, and landfill disposal. Relative to landfill disposal, reuse avoided approximately 5140 kg CO 2 -eq per t of pipeline for global warming potential (GWP), corresponding to an estimated upper bound of 1.34 billion kg CO 2 -eq from the decommissioning of 261,368.60 t of flexible pipelines in Brazil over the next decade, assuming that all pipelines still within their service lives are available for reuse. These findings show that the modeling perspective can reverse the environmental ranking of EoL options and that reusing remaining pipeline service life can reduce demand for new pipelines.

title: Bayesian optimization of exergy rate for multi-well injection schemes in carbon dioxide-based geothermal systems
abstract: Carbon dioxide-based geothermal systems use captured carbon dioxide as a subsurface working fluid, coupling renewable energy production with long-term carbon dioxide utilization. Their decades-long sustainability hinges on how carbon dioxide injection rates are allocated across wells and operational stages, yet each candidate strategy demands a computationally prohibitive full-physics simulation. With the lifetime average reservoir exergy rate as the objective, Bayesian optimization is employed to make this search tractable, identifying interpretable interwell injection-rate allocations while matching the solution quality of an industry-standard optimizer at a lower computational cost. The framework is demonstrated on a geothermal reservoir with five injectors and two producers over a 30-year lifetime, comparing Uniform, Zonal, and Stepwise Injection Rate Schemes against the lifetime average reservoir exergy rate. The results demonstrate that the exergy optimization primarily navigates a fundamental trade-off between the quantity and the quality of the produced energy. Excessive injection greatly penalizes performance, reducing the lifetime average exergy rate to 429 kW at a tenfold-higher rate, below the 494 kW obtained under conservative injection, which nonetheless underutilizes the reservoir. Temporal flexibility in the injection-rate allocation resolves this tension. Relative to the Zonal Rate Scheme, the Stepwise Rate Scheme raises specific exergy by 15.6% and cuts carbon dioxide injection by 11% while still delivering a higher average exergy rate, thereby extracting more useful energy from less carbon dioxide circulation. Flow diagnostics and Proper Orthogonal Decomposition analyses further confirm the underlying mechanism. Guided by the well connectivity, optimized injection-rate allocations redirect injection spatially and temporally, extending fluid residence time, whereas the geologically anchored dominant mode of the flow field remains unchanged. This study contributes essential insights into advancing sustainable energy production techniques, and the framework is generalizable to other subsurface systems involving multiple injection and production wells.

title: Uncertainty-aware PV-storage planning for EV fast-charging networks

Thermal physiology of Heterostegina depressa and its potential expansion in a warming Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Climate warming is reshaping the biogeography of the Mediterranean Sea and increasingly favours the establishment and range expansion of warm-affinity and non-indigenous species. We quantified the temperature dependence of physiological performance in Heterostegina depressa , a large benthic foraminifer that hosts obligate diatom symbionts, across 10–35 °C. Complementary measurements of photosynthetic performance, photosynthetically active area, chlorophyll-a and fucoxanthin, and assimilation of inorganic 13 C and 15 N revealed the highest overall performance around 25 °C and sustained activity between 20 and 30 °C, whereas both colder and warmer treatments strongly impaired host–symbiont functioning. These responses are consistent with previously reported thermal limits for H. depressa but extend them by integrating multiple physiological and metabolic endpoints. We combined the experimentally observed thermal window with Mediterranean seawater-temperature simulations to explore how the area thermally permissive for H. depressa may shift under warming. We interpret these maps as potential thermal suitability rather than predictions of realized distribution, because establishment also depends on light, depth, substrate, hydrodynamics, nutrient conditions, dispersal, and biotic interactions. The results place H. depressa within the broader tropicalization of Mediterranean biota, in which warming relaxes cold-season barriers for thermophilic taxa while increasing summer heat stress at the warm end of their thermal niche.

Renewable Energy Development and Fossil Fuel Displacement in the EU-27 Power Sector. A Dynamic and Decomposition-Based Approach
abstract: This study addresses the important and timely issue of energy transition in the EU-27 countries. Its aim is to assess the extent to which the development of renewable energy sources was accompanied by an absolute reduction in fossil fuel-based electricity generation in these countries over the period 2004–2024. The analysis considers the expansion of renewable energy sources (RES), the structural reconfiguration of the electricity generation mix, and the actual reduction in fossil fuel use. To this end, the study applies the Realized Fossil Displacement Ratio (RFDR), the Renewable Displacement Gap (RDG), balance decomposition, panel models with country and year fixed effects, technology- and fuel-specific heterogeneity analysis, panel local projections, an interaction model distinguishing between the periods 2005–2020 and 2021–2024, and a bootstrap sup-Wald threshold test. The results indicate that the substantial increase in renewable electricity generation was accompanied by a pronounced, though less than proportional, decline in fossil fuel-based electricity generation. The long-run RFDR amounted to 0.789, while the RDG accounted for approximately 21% of the cumulative increase in renewable electricity generation. The balance decomposition further showed that the decline in nuclear electricity generation corresponded to 31.26% of renewable generation growth, indicating that part of renewable expansion occurred in parallel with the loss of another low-carbon generation source rather than with an equivalent reduction in fossil fuel-based generation. The panel model revealed a negative but incomplete annual relationship, robust to alternative specifications. This relationship weakened over time, and its pattern in 2021–2024 differed significantly from that observed in the earlier period. Formal statistical tests did not provide sufficient evidence to confirm systematic heterogeneity across renewable energy technologies and fossil fuel types or the existence of a stable renewable-energy-share threshold common to the EU-27 countries. An increasing share of renewables should therefore not be treated as a stand-alone measure of fossil fuel displacement; instead, the progress of the energy transition should be assessed multidimensionally, taking into account changes in the electricity system as a whole .

Do the “Broadband China” strategy and social credit system construction enhance energy system resilience in the Yangtze River Delta?—Evidence from double machine learning and spatial spillover effects
abstract: Against the backdrop of frequent global energy conflicts and heightened uncertainty, ensuring the stability and resilience of the energy system has become a central challenge for the sustainable development of China's energy economy. The “Broadband China” strategy and social credit system construction can enhance the stability of the energy system by fostering technological innovation, strengthening market supervision, and providing external incentives. Accordingly, in this study, data from 41 prefecture-level cities in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) region from 2010 to 2022 were collected, and a double machine learning model combined with a spatial spillover effect model was used to explore the mechanisms through which the “Broadband China” strategy and the social credit system influence regional energy system resilience. The main findings are as follows: (1) During the study period, the overall resilience of the energy system in the YRD improved significantly and continued to grow rapidly. However, there were considerable disparities among cities, with larger improvements generally observed in eastern cities than in western cities. (2) Both the “Broadband China” strategy and social credit system construction significantly increased the resilience of the energy system in the YRD. (3) The energy system resilience in the YRD had a significant positive spatial spillover effect: The implementation of the “Broadband China” strategy in neighboring regions fostered improvements in local resilience, whereas social credit system construction in neighboring regions had no statistically significant effect.

title: Tail risk spillover effects of the technology market on Chinese new energy vehicle firms: A perspective of time-varying technological cycles
abstract: This study investigates the dynamic tail-risk connectedness and spillover effects from the global technology market to the Chinese New Energy Vehicle (NEV) industry. Amidst the global energy transition and heightened financial volatility, we employ a Conditional Autoregressive Value at Risk (CAViaR) model to quantify marginal tail risks, coupled with a Time-Varying Parameter Vector Autoregression (TVP-VAR) framework to construct dynamic risk spillover networks. Using daily data from January 2015 to March 2025, our analysis captures structural shifts in connectedness driven by critical technological cycles (e.g., the battery revolution and the emergence of disruptive AI models like DeepSeek) as well as exogenous shocks (e.g., the COVID-19 pandemic). Empirical findings reveal that tail-risk spillovers are highly asymmetric and time-varying. Notably, global technology markets serve as consistent net sources of tail-risk spillovers to the NEV sector, with network connectedness intensifying sharply during technological breakthroughs and macro-crises. Frequency-domain decomposition further demonstrates that while short-term spillovers dominate during tranquil periods, long-term tail-risk connectedness escalates significantly during crises. Additionally, leading NEV firms act as pivotal hubs in shaping intra-industry network dynamics. These findings elucidate the evolutionary patterns of tail-risk connectedness across distinct technological phases, providing actionable insights for dynamic portfolio allocation and risk management in the green economy.

title: AGORA cities: The hidden infrastructure shaping urban fragility
abstract: Urban services are unevenly distributed across the city, yet it is unclear when their joint presence signals fragility and when it instead outlines a neighbourhood’s vocation. For Bologna and Florence, we integrate Foursquare and OpenStreetMap points of interest with Sentinel-2-derived green indicators based on the 3–30–300 rule, cluster urban areas accordingly, and benchmark the clusters against the demographic, social, economic, and composite fragility indices produced by the municipal statistical offices, which are exogenous to the analysis. In both cities, we identify a subset of infrastructures, termed AGORA (Arts, Green environments, and Open Routes for Access and mobility), whose joint provision is associated with lower fragility. The AGORA Alignment score (AA), based on the rank correlation between AGORA endowment and composite fragility, indicates full alignment in Florence (AA = 1.00) and strong but incomplete alignment in Bologna (AA = 0.80). The remaining service categories instead show wide and heterogeneous distributions: they differentiate areas without tracking fragility and can be interpreted as expressions of urban vocations. The least fragile cluster, the only one with full AGORA endowment, hosts just 3.3% of residents in Bologna and 6.3% in Florence. The framework offers a procedure transferable to other contexts and identifies the expansion of AGORA infrastructures as a candidate lever for reducing fragility without altering existing vocations.

title: Rules without autonomy: environmental impact assessment as an institutional trap
Sustainable Development Index 2.0: An equity-based approach
Break‐even reference dependence in crop insurance decisions: Theory and evidence
abstract: Abstract We study farmers' crop insurance choices using a behavioral framework in which break‐even status serves as a salient, economically grounded, and empirically observable reference point. The framework nests the standard expected‐utility model as a special case and incorporates three forces: risk reduction, aversion to falling below break‐even status, and disutility from paying premiums. It yields sharp predictions about coverage choices, including bunching at the break‐even coverage level (BECL), defined as the coverage level where the insurance guarantee just covers total cost. We test these predictions using a survey of corn producers in Iowa and Kansas that elicits farmers' perceived BECLs, attitudes toward break‐even protection and premium costs, and their actual Federal Crop Insurance Program coverage choices. Coverage decisions display pronounced and asymmetric bunching around the BECL, with a sharp decline in frequency just below it and a smoother distribution above. Proxy measures of behavioral attitudes are also associated with observed choices in the predicted directions: farmers reporting stronger aversion to not breaking even are more likely to insure exactly at the BECL but not above it, while those reporting stronger premium aversion are more likely to insure below it. Using illustrative simulations, we further examine how subsidy changes interact with these behavioral forces and find that aversion to not breaking even may play an anchoring role that dampens the effects of premium subsidy cuts on coverage choices.

title: Should birds of a feather flock together: How public criticism shapes pressures for sustainability conformity and differentiation
abstract: Abstract Research Summary While firms face pressure to engage in Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices, it is unclear how they should specifically engage given the breadth of sustainability‐related concerns. Drawing on optimal distinctiveness and social evaluations research, we argue that public criticism directed toward an industry creates oscillating pressures for firms to conform with or deviate from industry ESG norms. Using data on 8176 global companies from 2013 to 2022, we find that although ESG conformity benefits investor evaluations, once industry peers' public criticism accumulates beyond a threshold, ESG differentiation is rewarded, particularly when firms increase material ESG practices and reduce immaterial ones. Our study reveals how public criticism dynamically reshapes the evaluative processes by which investors determine firm legitimacy, bridging optimal distinctiveness and social evaluations literatures. Managerial Summary Our research indicates that firms often adopt similar ESG practices as their industry peers, which usually enhances investor evaluations. However, this conformity can backfire and become a liability when industry peers face significant criticism. In such scenarios, firms that adopt distinctive ESG practices compared to the industry tend to receive greater rewards, especially when differentiation involves increasing material ESG practices and reducing immaterial ones. Therefore, while adopting ESG norms can be beneficial, managers should be vigilant of public opinion and ready to deviate from those norms when necessary.

title: Silent female representation and tech entrepreneurial project evaluation: The role of evaluators' genders
abstract: Abstract Research Summary We examine how the nature of female representation in tech entrepreneurial projects may be related to the evaluations of the projects. We argue that silent female representation —i.e., women are present but do not speak in representing projects—may reinforce the stereotyped view of women, resulting in lower project evaluations relative to male‐only projects, whereas active female representation may not lead to evaluation penalty. We further predict that the negative association between silent female representation and project evaluation is stronger when the evaluators are women than when they are men. Conducted in a unique setting wherein female and male evaluators on panels, independently and confidentially, rated funding applications represented by various mixes of male and female entrepreneurs, our study provides evidence that is consistent with these predictions. Managerial Summary It is widely recognized that female entrepreneurs face greater challenges than their male counterparts when seeking external financial resources in the tech sector. This funding disparity may start from evaluation disparity. We find that projects with silent female representation—i.e., women are present but do not speak—receive lower evaluations than male‐only projects, whereas projects with active female representation receive evaluations comparable to male‐only projects. We also find that female evaluators are more likely than male evaluators to penalize projects with silent female representation. Our research offers valuable insights into strategies for fostering gender equality in traditionally male‐dominated fields.

title: May I Have Your Attention, Please? Debating the Ontology of Attention in Organizational Research
abstract: Abstract Few constructs in management research have proved as generative as organizational attention, and few have been left so largely unexamined at their core. This Point‐Counterpoint debate brings a dormant question into the open: what exactly is attention? The Point argues for an ontological reorientation of the Attention‐Based View from attention quantity to attention quality, reconceptualizing attention as a set of sociomaterial practices of attending that are crescive and differentiated rather than limited and homogeneous. One Counterpoint defends the ontological integrity of attention as scarce, selective, and situated, warning that a crescive ontology dissolves the very constraint from which attention derives its explanatory power. The other Counterpoint charts an expansive third way, tracing the contested assumptions to Herbert Simon's legacy and proposing to broaden the Attention‐Based View towards competition, thicker situations, and possible attentional abundance. In this introduction to the debate, we present the three positions and reflect on what their disagreement teaches us about ontological disputes in management theory more generally. We distil three tests – of phenomena, of explanation, and of genealogy – that scholars can apply when deciding whether a construct's ontology deserves revision, defence, or expansion.

title: Place Matters: A Dynamic Multilevel Perspective on Stigma Management in French Elderly Care
abstract: Abstract This article interrogates how ‘place’ contributes to managing stigma and its associated multilevel processes. In doing so, it addresses a literature that often treats stigma as a static attribute, overlooking the spatial and material dynamics of managing it. Drawing on a 2.5‐year case study of Help@hom, a French national initiative aimed at restructuring elderly care, we examine how spatial and material arrangements actively shape stigma management processes. We identify three interrelated mechanisms – expanding , enclosing , and fragmenting – through which Help@hom reconfigures the meanings, locations, and materialities of care. Building on these mechanisms, we theorize place as producing, sustaining, and distributing the dynamics of stigma management: place produces stigma management strategies rather than merely providing their setting, sustains stigma by relocating rather than dissolving it, and distributes it across organizational, occupational, and individual levels. Our study demonstrates that place is constitutive of stigma management, shaping how organizations enact and experience multilevel stigma processes, and that spatial and material interventions can produce unexpected cross‐level consequences. In doing so, it advances recent efforts to conceptualize stigma as relational, dynamic, and systemic, and offers a more integrated understanding of how organizations navigate complex stigma management landscapes.

title: Impacts of hotel smart-digital applications on labour efficiency – A mixed-methods approach
Not all drivers are equal: An asymmetric framing of blockchain adoption
Exploring the Role of Cultural Capital in the Navigation of Religion-Based Stigma in the Workspace
abstract: Abstract Drawing on a study of 32 skilled Muslim humanitarian migrants, I show how cultural capital is discursively leveraged to navigate perceptions of religious stigma in the British workspace in a contested social process. Highlighting how the strategies used to navigate stigmatising connotations attached to religion (asserting worth, differentiating, aligning and minimising) are inscribed in embodied and institutionalised forms of cultural capital, I illustrate how stigma and privilege can coalesce in skilled individuals’ self-constructions. I draw attention to the tensions between the individual and the collective in individuals’ approaches to navigating religious stigma and its ethical implications. Finally, I theorise simultaneous engagement and disengagement as a crucial way of managing stigmatised religious affiliations, drawing attention to the temporal dimension of simultaneity and highlighting the performative nature of an Islamic religious identity.

title: Crash analysis of highway during full-length rehabilitation: A predictable and interpretable framework

Co-design and feasibility of an mHealth survivorship program for colorectal cancer survivors: a mix-methods study
abstract: Abstract Purpose Colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors experience persistent challenges that negatively affect health-related quality of life (HRQoL). While mobile health (mHealth) may offer a useful approach to survivorship care, limited user involvement and scarcity of structured programs in developing countries remain barriers. This study aimed to co-design and evaluate the feasibility of an mHealth survivorship program for CRC survivors following primary treatment. Methods A mixed-methods study was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 utilized a user-centered design framework involving 12 co-designers across nine online sessions to develop and refine the FORYOU mHealth program. Phase 2 was a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) with 30 CRC survivors to assess feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of the 12-week program, measured by HRQoL outcomes. Results In phase 1, the co-designed program indicated above-average usability (System Usability Scale ≥ 68) and adequate acceptability (E-Acceptability Scale ≥ 24). In phase 2, the adherence rate was 73.3%; participants in the intervention group completed an average of 5.4 out of 6 sessions and accessed the app 9.7 times. Although no significant between-group difference was observed in overall HRQoL, exploratory findings were mixed. The intervention favored the subscale functional well-being ( P < 0.05; g = 1.34), whereas the control group favored the secondary outcome, fatigue. These preliminary findings require cautious interpretation. Conclusion The co-designed mHealth program was usable and acceptable, and the pilot RCT was feasible among CRC survivors after primary treatment. Exploratory findings suggested possible benefits in selected outcomes, but these preliminary findings require confirmation in a larger adequately powered trial. Implications for Cancer Survivors This co-designed mHealth survivorship program showed encouraging engagement among CRC survivors after primary treatment, with exploratory findings suggesting potential effects on selected survivorship outcomes. Trial registration NCT07158671 on ClinicalTrials.gov. Registered on September 8, 2025

Cross-Domain Tracing of Rice Stem Stress under Soil Cadmium Pollution
abstract: Abstract Plants exposed to heavy-metal-contaminated soil are subjected to pollutant pressure, making timely monitoring of plant condition important for assessing their responses to soil pollution. Although spectral sensing is widely used for nondestructive monitoring of plant stress, the cross-domain association between plant optical signals and Cd-induced physiological responses remains unclear. Here, we integrated spectral sensing with deep learning, Monte Carlo simulation, and omics analysis to systematically explore how spectral signals and physiological responses jointly support the monitoring of Cd-induced stress in rice stems. We found that Cd exposure reorganized interface-associated stress, protective chemistry, and redox regulation into coordinated Defense, Repair, and Adjustment signatures. These biological changes were differentially expressed across the visible, red-edge, and near-infrared spectral regions, producing a reweighting of absorption- and scattering-sensitive information. The agreement between spectral variation and biological stress signatures further established a cross-domain link between stress-state formation and optical detection. Benefiting from this mechanism, we achieved high-accuracy nondestructive detection of rice stem Cd content and noninvasive characterization of Cd-induced responses. A portable spectrometer–smartphone implementation further demonstrated field-oriented feasibility. These findings provide a biological and optical basis for tracking stress progression and supporting timely, feedback-guided crop management.

title: Exploring the role of organics in sulfur autotrophic denitrification: Insights into community assembly and microbial co–occurrence
Form-dependent effects of silicon amendments on antibiotic resistance during vermicomposting: Insights into host bacteria and composting performance
Pyridinium-functionalized anion exchange resin for efficient removal of Cr(VI) in electroplating wastewater
Pooled accuracy does not transfer: validating kinetic and machine-learning models of wetland ammonium removal for design and compliance
abstract: Intensified treatment wetlands can achieve excellent total nitrogen (TN) removal, but their performance can be challenging to model with simple engineering approaches. We evaluated first-order kinetics, Monod kinetics, and machine learning (ML) across seven mature wetland configurations—vertical-flow wetlands (VFW) with gravel or sand media followed by woodchip and coconut husk bioreactors, and partially saturated vertical-flow (PSVF) systems with zeolite, gravel, or woodchip media—monitored over 12-21 months (2010-2023) at 8.8-25.1°C. All systems achieved 87.5-98.6% NH4+ and 73-89% TN removal. Aggregated ML analysis (n=176 sample events) achieved bootstrap R2=0.633 (95% CI: 0.479-0.742) for combined PSVF systems, but this aggregated metric masked overfitting when sample numbers were <15 (R2 = -0.30 to -9.69, where negative R2 indicates predictions worse than the sample mean). Kinetic approaches outperformed ML for 4 of 5 individual systems. Kinetic model fit ranged from R2=0.10-0.24 for high-efficiency VFW systems to R2=0.94 for PSVF configurations with distinct treatment zones (Monod). Stage-by-stage TN modelling revealed VFW nitrification stages contributed 17-22% of total TN removal, denitrifying woodchip bioreactors 59-81%, and polishing stages 9-12%. Predictive accuracy depended strongly on sample size, aggregation bias, removal efficiency (>95% creates ceiling effects), mechanism alignment, and design sizing. This analysis quantifies the boundary conditions for model applicability and demonstrates that aggregated ML metrics can misrepresent individual system performance. We provide a systematic model selection framework for routine prediction of operational performance in intensified treatment wetlands.

title: Microbial Inoculants and Substrate Amendments Restructure the Rhizosphere and Non‐Rhizosphere Microbial Communities in Saline‐Sodic Soil
abstract: ABSTRACT Microbial inoculants and organic substrates are effective measures for saline‐sodic soil remediation, but their individual and interactive effects across rhizosphere and non‐rhizosphere soils remain unclear. We evaluated three microbial inoculants (M1, M2, and M3), an organic substrate (B), and their combinations (BM1, BM2, and BM3) during two consecutive 45‐day Sesbania cannabina pot experiments. The substrate primarily promoted soil organic carbon accumulation, accounting for 57.31% of its variation, whereas inoculants explained more than 80% of the variation in pH and sodium adsorption ratio. M2 and BM2 increased mean plant biomass across the two growing seasons by 279.39% and 281.14%, respectively, relative to the control. Inoculants were also the dominant drivers of bacterial community structure, explaining 18.05% and 18.78% of the variation in non‐rhizosphere and rhizosphere soils, respectively, compared with 3.71% and 3.40% for the substrate. Treatment effects were compartment dependent: M2 was associated with greater microbial network robustness, whereas M3 and BM3 enriched bacterial taxa and predicted functions related to carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycling. Overall, microbial inoculants and organic substrates contributed distinctly but complementarily to saline‐sodic soil amelioration, with inoculants primarily regulating salinity‐related properties and microbial communities and the substrate mainly enhancing soil carbon accumulation.

title: Surveilled bodies, normalized violence: Migrant women’s everyday experiences with digital-material surveillance in Singapore
abstract: This paper examines how digital monitoring operates alongside face-to-face surveillance across socio-material-digital spaces, as contemporary migration to Singapore intersects with intensifying digital surveillance. Focusing on two non-elite, working-class groups of migrant women – migrant domestic workers and marriage migrants married to Singaporean men – we illustrate how entangled digital and non-digital surveillance practices produce gendered precarity through the mundane violence of everyday monitoring in both public and private spheres. We draw on qualitative interview and ethnographic data to demonstrate how surveillance reconfigures gendered boundaries of care and control while normalizing everyday violence against migrant bodies. Crucially, we reveal the ambivalent nature of surveillance as both a mechanism of control and a domain of migrant agency. Women experience and comply with surveillance to be seen as “good migrants,” while simultaneously engaging in lateral surveillance and reverse surveillance as tactics of negotiation and resistance. Ultimately, we argue that the normalization of hybrid surveillance conducts political work within Singapore’s constrained public spheres, producing working-class migrant women as active surveillance subjects whose sense of belonging remains deeply conditional.

title: Poxviruses probably evolved in the digestive system of animals
abstract: Large and giant DNA viruses that infect unicellular eukaryotes are abundant in the environment but have rarely been found in the gut microbiome. The discovery of such viruses that prevail in the digestive system of humans and animals exposes a long-overlooked facet of the gut microbiome that clarifies the origin of poxviruses. Newly discovered viruses distributed in animal digestive systems are the closest known relatives of the clade containing smallpox virus.

title: First observation of a giant star swallowing its neighbour

Kings of the jungle? This early human had surprising survival skills that rivalled ours
Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems
Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
abstract: Abstract Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps 1,2 . These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass 3 but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds 3 , suggesting that their magnetic sense 4 probably harnesses the Earth’s magnetic field as a compass. However, the nature of this compass, and of the magnetic sense underlying it, remains unknown. Here we show that Bogong moths, tethered in a flight arena under a full-spectrum randomized starry night sky, navigate in their inherited migratory direction using the geomagnetic field alone. If the geomagnetic field is turned by 180°, or if inclination is inverted, moths fly in the opposite direction. If polarity is inverted, moths fail to turn. Furthermore, if violet–blue light (380 nm < λ < 500 nm) is removed from the illumination spectrum, or if tethered moths are exposed to weak broadband radiofrequency fields (150 kHz to 60 MHz), magnetic orientation is abolished. Our results indicate that Bogong moths use the geomagnetic field as an inclination compass for long-distance navigation at night and possess a light-dependent radical-pair-based magnetic sense 5 .

title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
abstract: Hominin fossils and genetic evidence indicate that several hominin populations occupied East and Southeast Asia during the Middle and Late Pleistocene epoch1–10. Homo erectus fossils remain scarce in southern China and mainland Southeast Asia4,8,11. Here we report nine newly discovered late Middle Pleistocene hominin teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves at the Chongzuo study area, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, southern China, dated to around 324–184 thousand years ago12. Palaeoproteomics reveals the presence of an endogenous dental proteome in all five hominin teeth studied molecularly. Four teeth contain a derived H. erectus substitution in ameloblastin that to date has been observed only in older Middle Pleistocene H. erectus specimens from China13. The proteomes of these four teeth differ from the previous H. erectus proteomes from China at another ameloblastin position, suggesting that these specimens represent a previously unsampled H. erectus population. Morphometric and geometric morphometric methods support an attribution of these teeth to H. erectus, as well as four additional teeth. This fills a gap in the geographical and chronological distribution of H. erectus in East Asia. The fifth tooth studied proteomically, PA1796, is morphologically distinct from H. erectus, Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis) and modern humans (Homo sapiens), and does not contain the H. erectus-derived amino acid sequence. The late survival of H. erectus on mainland East Asia suggests that at least two hominin lineages, H. erectus and Homo longi (Denisovans)6,7, possibly represented by PA1796, were present in the region towards the end of the Middle Pleistocene, with the first documented occurrence of H. sapiens not much later5. Late Middle Pleistocene hominin teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves of southern China, dated to around 324–184 thousand years ago, fill a gap in the geographical and chronological distribution of Homo erectus in East Asia.

title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
abstract: Homo erectus represents one of the longest-persisting hominin species, with a geographic range from Africa to eastern Eurasia from approximately 1.9 million years ago 1 to 108 thousand years ago (ka) 2 . Despite this, there are still large gaps in our understanding of the adaptation capabilities of this species and the extent of its persistence in China. Assumptions over ecological preferences based on the Trinil 3 , Sangiran 4 and Ngandong 2 (in Java) open woodland–grassland mosaics have persisted, combined with limited direct stable carbon isotope measurements in Asia. Here we present a rich temporal and environmental context for nine hominin teeth, eight of which were morphologically and genetically identified as H. erectus 5 , found in two sister caves in Guangxi province, southern China. We modelled 43 radiometric ages from five dating techniques to establish a timeline for H. erectus presence in this region. Stable and clumped isotopes and trace elements from teeth were used to establish the dominant environments and their behavioural responses. We show that H. erectus was present in southern China between 324 and 184 ka, which is substantially more recent than previously established in this region for unequivocally H. erectus fossils at approximately 400 ka. The evidence suggests that they were persisting in closed rainforest ecosystems, thought to be the domain of only Homo sapiens , and were demonstrating long-term mobility and ecological flexibility. This evidence challenges the assumptions over the ecological preferences and behavioural limitations of H. erectus .

title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
abstract: Abstract Quantum field theories provide fundamental models of complex interacting systems 1–3 , from high-energy physics and cosmology to condensed matter. However, solving these models in non-perturbative and dynamical regimes is often challenging, particularly in more than one spatial dimension. Analogue simulation using tunable synthetic quantum systems can both verify existing theoretical predictions and lead to physical insights. Here we realize analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions (two spatial dimensions and time), using two coherently coupled spin components 4,5 in a uniform two-dimensional atomic Bose–Einstein condensate 6,7 . Specifically, we encode the paradigmatic sine-Gordon model 8,9 in the long-wavelength modes of the field describing the relative phase, ϕ , of the two components. In the perturbative regime, collective field excitations exhibit a relativistic dispersion with a tunable mass gap. We also observe explicitly non-perturbative phenomena, including the existence of topological domain walls across which ϕ rapidly winds by 2π (ref. 10 ). Our work opens possibilities for studies of cosmologically relevant phenomena including preheating 11,12 , dynamics of topological defects 13,14 and relativistic false-vacuum decay 15–19 .

title: Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies
Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
abstract: Abstract One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p -wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1–3 ). Achieving p -wave superconductivity 4 and its magnetic analogue 5 —characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p -wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge 6,7 . Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p -wave magnets 5,7–10 , spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p -wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p -wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves S y polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted S y exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p -wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p -wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics 10 , topological matter 7 , superconductivity 11 and beyond.

title: Quantum position verification with remote untrusted devices
Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum
abstract: Abstract The genus Hordeum comprises cultivated barley and its wild relatives, an evolutionarily, ecologically and agriculturally important group of grasses 1,2 . Here we generated a chromosome-scale comparative genomic resource comprising all recognized diploid Hordeum species together with representative polyploid lineages. Comparative analyses reveal extensive structural variation, including inversions and chromosomal rearrangements that disrupt proximal collinearity and reflect lineage-specific genome remodelling. Single-copy gene phylogenies identify ancient hybridization, segmental exchange and introgression, revealing pervasive reticulate evolution during Hordeum diversification. We uncover widespread horizontal gene transfer from Panicoideae grasses into Hordeum , with many transferred genes showing evidence of transcription and functional integration. Retrotransposon proliferation explains genome size variation and provides insights into polyploid genome evolution. Whole-genome alignments reveal contrasting evolutionary dynamics: whereas coding sequences remain highly conserved, regulatory elements undergo rapid turnover, providing a rich source of regulatory diversity for phenotypic evolution. Case studies of vernalization and glume development demonstrate how natural variation in regulatory and coding sequences contributes to flowering time and floral morphology. This comprehensive pangenomic framework establishes Hordeum as a model for studying genome evolution, structural variation and the genetic basis of adaptive traits, offering new avenues for barley improvement.

title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
abstract: Abstract Resistance in standard conductors decreases with increasing cross-section. Yet, in low-dimensional superconductors and superfluids, residual resistance arises from topological fluctuations of the order parameter, manifesting as phase slips in one-dimensional (1D) and vortices in two-dimensional (2D) systems. How resistance and dissipation evolve as geometry interpolates between these regimes remains an open question. This evolution is masked in solid-state experiments by disorder, impurities and geometric imperfections 1–3 , and poses theoretical challenges due to competing dissipative processes and pronounced finite-size effects. Here, we use a defect-free unitary Fermi gas in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox: in the crossover from one dimension to two dimensions, the resistance reaches a minimum. There, widening a channel increases its resistance. Narrower, quasi-1D channels show dissipation described by Langer–Ambegaokar–McCumber–Halperin theory of phase slips 4 . In this regime, varying the channel width yields the predicted exponential scaling of the activation factor over many orders of magnitude. Wider, quasi-2D channels show dissipation consistent with phase-slip events described by a finite-size vortex model 5 . The minimal dissipation in the dimensional crossover reflects a transition in the dominant dissipative mechanism, with both 1D and 2D events simultaneously suppressed. Our measurements suggest a route to minimizing dissipation in superconducting devices and provide a benchmark for theoretical efforts aimed at describing the dimensional crossover.

title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity
abstract: Abstract Tropical land-use intensification threatens global biodiversity, yet most assessments of tropical agricultural landscapes focus on local-scale biodiversity, overlooking how land use restructures biodiversity across space and multiple taxa. Here we provide an ecosystem-wide assessment of 24 taxonomic groups across all domains of life—encompassing 40,049 species—along a land-use intensification gradient from lowland forests to intensively managed smallholder cash-crop monocultures in Indonesian landscapes. Despite widespread losses of landscape and local multidiversity 1 in monocultures (approximately 78% and 50%, respectively), we found no evidence for consistent community homogenization with land-use intensification. Instead, monocultures exhibit a systematic shift from turnover to nestedness for aboveground taxa. Such patterns of differentiation may mask trajectories towards biotic homogenization via early stages of assemblage simplification. Biotic differentiation has the potential to partly mitigate biodiversity losses by positively affecting γ-diversity. This opens management options, including the conservation of existing remnants of traditional agriculture and the implementation of sustainable management practices 2–4 . Our results demonstrate that tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity not only through species loss, but also via a pervasive reorganization of community composition across trophic levels. Conserving tropical biodiversity, therefore, requires a multi-taxon, landscape-scale perspective that explicitly integrates agricultural land uses with the protection of natural and semi-natural habitats to reconcile agricultural production and conservation.

title: TransA-MERFISH reveals divergent post-retinal direction-selective circuits
abstract: A major goal in neuroscience is to map the transformation of information as it flows through the brain. For example, neurons at many levels of the visual hierarchy are attuned to motion direction1–5. However, links between motion-selective computations and cell types at various stages of the visual hierarchy remain unidentified. A key first step in delineating these relationships is to map the wiring diagrams that connect different motion-selective cell types. Here we establish a systematic, cell-type-specific circuit-mapping method, combining an anterograde trans-neuronal fluorescent tracer (mWGA–mCherry)6 with spatial transcriptomics (multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH))7,8 to establish TransA-MERFISH. We used TransA-MERFISH to comprehensively map the synaptic target cell types of four retinal ganglion cell subclasses in superior colliculus (SC) at cell-type resolution. These experiments unexpectedly revealed that retinal on–off direction-selective ganglion cells (ooDSGCs) innervate several direction-selective SC cell types, but do not innervate a SC cell type that was previously reported to display strong direction-selective responses. We validated these results using orthogonal approaches and demonstrated the sensitivity and specificity of TransA-MERFISH. Functional studies of SC activity before and after ablation of retinal direction-selective circuits confirmed that these computationally distinct, ooDSGC-dependent and -independent direction-selective cell types are commingled in SC. Together, our study establishes TransA-MERFISH as a robust framework for mapping wiring diagrams at the cell-type level and uncovers divergent computational mechanisms of motion detection in early visual processing. TransA-MERFISH combines anterograde trans-neuronal tracing and spatial transcriptomics and reveals distinct retinal on–off direction-selective ganglion cell-dependent and independent motion-selective pathways in superior colliculus, establishing a sensitive cell-type-resolved framework for wiring-diagram reconstruction in early visual processing.

title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions
Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues
abstract: The intestinal mucosal barrier contains microbial organisms within the lumen while preserving the ability to absorb nutrients. Dietary, microbial, and other exposures shaped human barrier evolution and continue to impact disease susceptibility. Here, we established engineered barrier models of the human small intestine and colon composed of a multilineage epithelium, mucus layer, accessible microbial compartment and autologous tissue-resident immune cells. The epithelium has crypt- and villus-like topological domains, with stem cells differentiating into absorptive and secretory lineages with region-specific identities. Secreted mucins accumulate apically, forming a dense mucus layer separating the epithelium from colonizing commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Intestinal memory T cells integrate into and interact with the epithelium. We use the engineered intestinal tissues to identify an epithelial gene regulatory network underlying response to Salmonella Typhimurium infection, and uncover epithelial-immune-pathogen crosstalk coordinating cytokine release and epithelial damage. Overall, this work allows for the modular integration of epithelial, microbial, and immune compartments providing a versatile system for studying human intestinal physiology and pathologies.

title: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs
Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE2 production for tumour immune escape
abstract: Abstract Ferroptosis, a form of cell death induced by overwhelming membrane lipid peroxidation, is a vulnerability of many cancers, including cancers resistant to current molecular and immune-based therapies 1–7 . Triggering of ferroptosis therefore provides an opportunity to achieve elimination of difficult-to-treat cancers 1–4,8,9 . Studies in mouse cancer models have demonstrated that anticancer immunity, mediated by dendritic cells (DCs) and CD8 + T cells, is essential for effective tumour eradication by ferroptosis-inducing strategies 10–13 . However, ferroptotic cells limit this response 8–10,14 , resulting in immune escape and tumour growth through mechanisms that remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program resulting in aberrant production of prostaglandin E 2 (PGE 2 ), which limits the stimulation of anticancer CD8 + T cell responses by type 1 conventional DCs (cDC1s), thereby promoting immune escape. In ferroptotic cancer cells, lipid peroxidation-mediated membrane permeabilization enables Ca 2+ influx, which activates p38 MAPK signalling and thereby drives PGE 2 production. This signalling axis is uncoupled from cancer cell death and can be targeted to selectively interfere with immune-inhibitory PGE 2 production while preserving ferroptotic cancer cell elimination. In the context of cancer cell ferroptosis, ablation of PGE 2 production or disrupting PGE 2 signalling restores cDC1-mediated anticancer CD8 + T cell responses and leads to effective tumour elimination. Our findings identify a key mechanism that limits antitumour immunity and prevents tumour elimination upon ferroptosis induction in cancer cells, which could be exploited for cancer therapy.

title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
abstract: Abstract Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing 1 . Yet, their practical implementation remains limited by the intrinsically weak optical nonlinearities of conventional materials, which demand high power and large device footprints to achieve substantial nonlinear responses 2 . Exciton–polaritons, hybrid light–matter excitations of semiconducting materials, offer a promising route to overcome these limitations by combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability typical of photonic platforms 3–5 . However, despite their potential, fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification have remained elusive. Here we demonstrate a fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings these functionalities together in a single-step-grown platform. We realize precise and scalable polariton circuits with integrated gratings that act as both couplers and reflectors, enabling in-plane Fabry–Pérot cavities. These structures support robust in-plane polariton lasing with coherent guided emission at a geometry-defined wavelength, optical amplification of propagating polaritons and nonlinear optical phase control exceeding π, all within the same on-chip architecture. Our results establish perovskite polariton circuits as a scalable platform for active and interferometric integrated photonics.

title: Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands
abstract: Abstract Islands harbor a disproportionate share of global biodiversity 1 , yet insects, even invaluable pollinators such as bees 2 , remain underrepresented in island biogeography research 3 . Here, we present the first global checklist of island bees, recording 4,140 species across 306 islands. Although islands comprise only ∼5% of Earth’s land area, they support ∼20% of global bee diversity, and 43% of insular species are endemic, making up ∼8% of all known bee species. Island bee species richness, mirroring continental trends 4 , peaks at mid-latitudes. Native richness increases with island area and declines with isolation, consistent with patterns in other taxa 5 . The strength of species–area relationships varies among biomes and is steepest in mediterranean-type systems, which also support disproportionately high bee richness relative to flowering plant diversity. Endemism is highest on large tropical islands, reflecting extensive in situ diversification. Major centers of bee endemism include Madagascar, Malesia (e.g. the Greater Sundas and New Guinea), and Hawai’i, where a single large radiation of Hylaeus ( Nesoprosopis ) dominates 6 . Among islands capable of supporting endemic species, endemism scales strongly with total richness. These findings highlight the need to integrate island bee diversity into global conservation planning and position bees as a model for understanding insect evolution and conservation on islands.

title: Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites
Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
abstract: Abstract Large and giant double-stranded DNA viruses substantially affect eukaryotic ecology and evolution 1–4 . They prevail in the environment but are rarely found in the digestive system of animals 5,6 . Here we present the discovery of a diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes, dubbed egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses. Egoviruses are found worldwide, almost exclusively in the digestive system of humans, livestock and wild animals. The most prevalent human-specific egovirus is spread across continents, demonstrating a long-term association between egoviruses and the human gut microbiome. Eukaryotic homologues of egovirus core genes suggest that these viruses primarily infect Trichostomatia (ciliates), which assist ruminant digestive processes 7 , and Parabasalia (Metamonada), which influence animal immunity and gut microbiome ecology 8 . Egoviruses also contributed to the genetic makeup of polintons, endogenous viruses that proliferated in genomes of Trichomonas vaginalis 9 and its close Parabasalia relatives. Unlike poxviruses that form brick-shaped virions, egoviruses are predicted to form multilayered icosahedral capsids resembling those of asfuviruses and probably representing the ancestral virion structure. Egoviruses are the only known clade of double-stranded DNA viruses of eukaryotes prevailing in the animal digestive system. Phylogenomic analysis suggests an evolutionary scenario whereby egovirus-like ancestors of poxviruses infected anaerobic unicellular eukaryotes inside the gut of ancestral animals, before transitioning to animal cell infection, which was accompanied by the virion metamorphosis.

title: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts
abstract: Abstract Cannibalism, the consumption of conspecifics, is widespread across the animal kingdom and can profoundly influence individual fitness and population dynamics 1,2 . Although the ecological and social conditions that favour cannibalism have been well documented 2 , the molecular signals that trigger cannibalistic attacks have remained poorly understood. Here we show that in Locusta migratoria , guaiacol, a volatile compound with augmented release after injury, attracts gregarious nymphs and induces cannibalistic behaviour. Guaiacol is detected by olfactory receptors LmOR36 and LmOR34, and disruption of either receptor abolishes attraction, thereby impairing induction of cannibalism. Guaiacol is synthesized by haemolymph symbiont Enterobacter hormaechei . Injury promotes bacterial congregation at the wound site, leading to elevated guaiacol production through a clustered set of vanillic acid decarboxylase genes; deletion of this gene cluster abolishes guaiacol production and its behavioural effects. Notably, guaiacol initially functions as a beneficial signal after injury. Guaiacol activates immune-related pathways in wounded locusts, enhancing pathogen resistance and increasing survival following minor injury. However, when guaiacol emission exceeds a threshold determined by injury severity, it functions as an external cue that attracts cannibals. Cannibalistic locusts exploit this immune-related odour to locate severely injured conspecifics, gaining both nutritional resources and immune system benefits. Together, our findings identify a microbial–chemical mechanism that links immune defence with cannibalistic behaviour and provide potential molecular targets for manipulation of cannibalism-dependent population dynamics.

title: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: . These fundamental processes are regulated by the hypothalamus, yet how its functionally distinct subregions and cell types change during human ageing and Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains largely unexplored. Here we present HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, including high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei from young participants, patients with AD and age-matched non-dementia control participants. We show that hypothalamic subregions governing metabolism, stress and circadian rhythms are particularly vulnerable, showing notable changes in both volumes and gene expression during ageing and AD. At the molecular level, machine learning models identified the inflammatory response and regulators of circadian rhythms as key cellular predictors of AD. These signatures were reflected in specific cell types: microglia transitioned to a pro-inflammatory state, whereas inhibitory neurons within sleep-regulating and circadian-regulating hypothalamic subregions showed the most profound transcriptional alterations, including disruptions in ligand-receptor interactions and G-protein-coupled receptor signalling. HypoAD provides a high-resolution volumetric map and a transcriptomic atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, relating lifestyle and behavioural changes to the relevant volumetric and molecular pathways. In addition, HypoAD provides a framework to investigate hypothalamic dysfunction and establishes a roadmap for targeted interventions aimed at mitigating physiological disruptions to potentially slow disease progression.

title: Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species
abstract: Current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation 1 . Given the breadth and diversity of human tumour pathology and contributions of tumour microenvironment (TME) cells to disease progression, pan-cancer analysis is needed to bridge major themes of stromal and immune cell evolution. To date, however, efforts to compare the TME response across cancers have been limited in scope 2 , 3 . Here we conduct a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis by algorithmically screening thousands of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets for stromal and immune signatures across species and tissue types. We demonstrate conserved hallmarks of host cell transcriptional programming in response to malignancy across 42 cancer types in more than 2,000 human and mouse tumour samples. These findings are codified as an interactive web atlas ( tmeatlas.stanford.edu ) and software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for the systematic interrogation of the TME in tumours.

title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
abstract: Abstract van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies 1–4 . Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases 2,5,6 . However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space 7–12 ), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

title: Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin
Injured locusts heal or are cannibalized depending on levels of a bacterial odour molecule
abstract: When migratory locusts are injured, an odorous chemical produced by bacteria living in or on their bodies activates the immune system, helping them to fight disease-causing agents. However, when a wound is large and the chemical becomes too concentrated, it attracts cannibalistic locusts. At low levels, guaiacol promotes immune function; at high levels, it prompts other locusts to eat their swarm-mate.

Tropical land-use intensification reshapes biodiversity in expected and unexpected ways
abstract: Global agricultural demand has increased over the past few decades, driving land-use intensification in some of the world’s most biodiverse regions. An assessment of some 40,000 species, from soil microorganisms to vertebrates, in Sumatra, Indonesia, reveals that agricultural intensification threatens biodiversity through species loss and changes in community composition across different spatial scales. A survey of 40,000 species in Sumatra, Indonesia, could inform conservation efforts.

From Design to Disclosure
abstract: Abstract We study the role of hard information in contractual and market settings in which the receiver can flexibly adjust allocations and transfers in response to the sender's disclosure. These settings include monopoly pricing, insurance contracting, and policy negotiations. Across these settings, the sender is worst off if she reveals her type completely because the receiver would then adjust the terms of trade to extract her surplus. Taking this feature as our central departure from the literature, we characterize the entire set of equilibrium payoffs in these disclosure games. We prove an equivalence result: a payoff profile can be approximated by an equilibrium of the disclosure game if and only if it can be achieved through information design. Thus, there exist equilibria in which the sender obtains approximately her commitment payoff.

Enhancing portfolio resilience to systemic risk: A neural network approach
abstract: This paper aims to enhance the classical mean–variance portfolio selection model by using machine learning techniques and accounting for systemic risk. The optimal portfolio is obtained through a three-step supervised learning model. Firstly, the Smooth Pinball Neural Network is employed to predict return distributions of individual assets and the market. Secondly, we use a copula to model dependence between assets and the market, based on which we simulate return scenarios. Lastly, we maximize an ex-ante Sharpe ratio conditioning on systemic events. We train our models using a comprehensive dataset of nearly 600 U.S. individual stocks over 37 years; however, the portfolio analysis and backtesting are conducted on several representative portfolio sets with sizes up to 50 assets. This design allows the models to learn from a broad cross-section of firms while focusing the evaluation on computationally tractable portfolio dimensions. Our set of predictors includes 94 firm characteristics, 14 macroeconomic variables, and 74 industry dummies. The backtesting results demonstrate the superiority of our proposed approach over popular benchmark strategies including a GARCH-based model. This outperformance is statistically significant and robust to the inclusion of transaction costs.

title: Expertise, signaling and learning in fish auctions
abstract: Theoretical analyses have demonstrated that in sequential auctions, prices follow a martingale. Yet, empirical observations often indicate varied price points for comparable products. We examine sales of fresh seafood through sequential Dutch auctions at the Sydney Fish Market (SFM), presenting evidence of non-monotonic price trends and investigating the causes of price variations among homogeneous products. With the extensive data set covering over 27 years of transactions at SFM, we address potential endogeneity concerns arising from seafood diversity. Employing the lot fixed-effects approach to standardize transactions, we discern bidding patterns that differ according to bidders’ experience levels. Additionally, our findings highlight evidence of signaling and learning. We infer that the agents’ heterogeneity in the market creates an interactive environment: bidders tend to bid higher when following an experienced leader, but this trend reverses when the initial bid comes from someone not experienced, highlighting how bidders adjust based on signals from others.

Can Developing Economies Implement SCC-Aligned Carbon Pricing? Evidence from Vietnam’s Pilot ETS under EU CBAM
From paradigms to instruments: ideational constraints on industrial policy and the Dutch National Growth Fund
abstract: The resurgence of industrial policy has sparked debate over whether contemporary state intervention marks a break with neoliberalism or rather its reconfiguration. We add nuance by shifting the focus from macro-level paradigms to meso-level instruments, developing an analytical framework for mapping industrial policy instruments based on two key dimensions: selectivity, the degree to which the state directs investment toward specific sectors, and conditionality, the discipline attached to public support. Neoliberal settings, such as those prevalent in high-income economies, encompass competing ideational currents with different views on these dimensions: Pro-business neoliberals favor selectivity to support competitive firms while placing less emphasis on conditionality, whereas frugal neoliberals prioritize conditionality to discipline public spending but are skeptical about selectivity. Instrument design reflects the negotiation between these competing currents. We illustrate this argument through a case study of the Dutch National Growth Fund, based on 24 semi-structured interviews and documentary analysis. We find that the dominance of frugal neoliberal ideas produced an instrument shaped more by conditionality than selectivity, suggesting that recent industrial policy initiatives have been bounded by intra-neoliberal contestation. The article contributes a meso-level analytical framework for analyzing variation in industrial policy design across high-income economies.

title: The international fragmentation of financial production
abstract: Since the 1990s, service sectors have expanded significantly, surpassing manufacturing in most economies. This shift has occurred alongside the rise of global value chains (GVCs), with an increasing share of trade involving intermediate services. However, existing GVC literature has largely overlooked the global fragmentation of financial services. This work addresses this gap by applying a GVC perspective to the international organization of financial production. We provide an exploratory analysis of the fragmentation and positioning of the Financial and Insurance (FI) sector between 1995 and 2020. Using Inter-Country Input-Output (ICIO) data, we trace cross-border flows of intermediate financial services and map the emerging global hierarchy across advanced and emerging economies. Our findings show that, unlike manufacturing GVCs, which have stagnated since the 2008 crisis, the international fragmentation of financial production has continued to expand. Within this process, the United Kingdom’s financial sector has consolidated an increasing upstream position in global financial chains, allowing it to appropriate a growing share of value embodied in international trade flows. These results shed new light on the spatial organization of financial services and the uneven value capture opportunities across countries, opening new research avenues on global hierarchies within the GVCs of the financial industry.

title: Climate Policy and Sovereign Debt: The Impact of Transition Scenarios on Sovereign Creditworthiness
abstract: Abstract This paper links climate science with sovereign risk assessment to produce a single forward-looking measure of country-level climate change risk. We combine the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) climate scenarios with a sovereign credit ratings model to simulate the impact of climate change on credit ratings, cost of debt and probability of default. For the first time, we extend beyond the physical risks of extreme weather events to explicitly incorporate risks associated with transitioning the global economy towards Net Zero. Across the sample of 48 countries and under a scenario of high (low) physical and transition risks, we find average increases in the cost of debt of 61 (31) basis points and default probability of 4.7% (2.4%). Counter-intuitively, ratings, default probability, and cost of debt appear insensitive to scenarios in some countries, with important implications for the usefulness of NGFS scenarios across central banks.

title: Civilisational capitalism: the economic thinking of the European New Right
abstract: This paper brings discussions about far-right political economy into dialogue with the history of ideas by examining the economic thinking of the radical right intellectual movement known as the European New Right (ENR). We reconstruct the economic visions proposed by the ENR intellectuals Alain de Benoist, Guillaume Faye, Jean Thiriart, and Alexander Dugin. Despite notable differences, a common set of themes traverses their thinking: a spiritual critique of capitalism as a materialist ‘market society’; a producerism that elevates a notion of domestic industrial and entrepreneurial capitalism over transnational, financial, or managerial capitalism; a commitment to the autarky of civilisational blocs or ‘great spaces’; and a notion of an ‘organic economy’. For all four thinkers, the free market should be limited externally through new geopolitical arrangements and internally through organising domestic economies around the spiritual purpose of the ‘civilisation’ in question. Yet all imagine that the destructive tendencies of globalised capitalism can be overcome while maintaining its central institutions of private property and commodified labour. Envisioning a post-liberal world order organised into a patchwork of culturally continuous civilisational blocs, we propose that the ENR’s economic visions can be characterised as forms of ‘civilisational capitalism’.

title: Forecast Accuracy and Efficiency at the Bank of England
abstract: ABSTRACT We propose a systematic approach for central banks to leverage past forecasts (and associated errors) with the aim of learning more about the structure and functioning of the underlying economy. Applying this method to forecasts made by the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee since 2011, we find that its forecasts have tended to underestimate the inflationary consequences of real wage growth, while also underestimating the inflationary consequences of real GDP growth in the near term. Regarding the effects of monetary policy, our results are, for example, consistent with transmission via inflation expectations having played a bigger role than attributed to it in the forecast. This may point to a more favourable sacrifice ratio.

title: The Consequences of Pay Standing under Pay Range Transparency
abstract: Pay range transparency—that is, disclosing the minimum and maximum pay for a job rather than individuals’ actual pay—has become the most prevalent form of pay transparency. Yet, existing theories explain employee reactions to pay information through present-focused, interpersonal comparisons with coworkers’ pay. We theorize that pay range transparency instead directs employees to interpret their structural pay standing—their pay position relative to the disclosed range boundaries—as a forward-looking signal of the organization’s recognition and structural room for pay growth. Drawing on expectancy theory, we propose that structural pay standing has a curvilinear (attenuated-positive) effect on job satisfaction, intention to stay, and job performance, mediated by pay growth uncertainty: pay near the range minimum offers weak evidence that contributions will be recognized, whereas pay near the maximum reveals limited structural room for further growth, a pattern we term a ceiling effect. Pay-related procedural justice attenuates these effects. Four studies—a natural experiment (n = 371), an online experiment (n = 603), a three-wave field study (n = 525), and an experimental-causal-chain study (n = 392)—support our theorizing, establishing structural pay standing as distinct from interpersonal pay standing and revealing an unrecognized trade-off of pay range transparency.

title: The entrepreneur as ecosystem architect: Economic foundations for strategic entrepreneurship in the age of AI
abstract: Abstract Research Summary This paper develops an alternative foundation for understanding strategic entrepreneurship in the age of artificial intelligence (AI) by joining entrepreneurship research with the profiting from innovation model and the dynamic capabilities framework. It argues that the economic function of the entrepreneur is increasingly that of an ecosystem architect, exercising judgment under uncertainty to orchestrate complementary assets and capabilities across organizational boundaries.
