Ionization, Latitude, and Altitude Dependence of Particle Formation in Stratospheric SO 2 and H 2 S Injection Plumes
abstract: Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) has received increasing attention as a potential temporary climate intervention strategy. A critical source of uncertainty involves subgrid processes within injection plumes─specifically new particle formation (NPF)─which influence particle size distribution and overall SAI efficacy. This work provides the first comprehensive modeling study of NPF and size distribution evolution within subgrid aircraft plumes at tropical and subpolar sites for both sulfur dioxide (SO2) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) SAI. Results indicate that H2S SAI generally produces new particles as effectively as SO2 SAI when the precursor mass injection rate is the same. Notably, due to a much higher ionization rate, subpolar regions exhibit higher particle formation efficiency and less condensation on background aerosols compared to tropical areas. Without considering the ionization effect, NPF in the subpolar SO2 and H2S SAI plumes is negligible. Furthermore, NPF efficacy diminishes sharply with increasing injection altitude, a trend driven by changing ionization rates and other parameters at higher elevations. The analysis also highlights that particle creation efficiency is strongly affected by other factors. The insights gained contribute to more informed decision-making regarding climate intervention strategies and governance.

title: High-Throughput Hazard Identification Reveals Cardiac and Developmental Toxicity of Liquid Crystal Monomers toward Zebrafish
abstract: The rapid proliferation of chemicals (e.g., liquid crystal monomers (LCMs)) threatens human and ecosystem health, necessitating urgent hazard identification. Traditional morphological analysis involves tedious manual work and inconsistent estimation. Herein, we established a workflow and three software platforms for automated quantitative analysis of chemical-induced zebrafish phenotypes and cardiac effects by combining the high-content imaging system with the YOLOv8 deep learning method. The segmentation models with mask precision and bounding box precision >0.990 for zebrafish phenotypes (eye, head, pericardium, yolk sac, body, atrium and ventricle) outperform existing models. The analysis of phenotypes and cardiac function of 14 LCMs based on built methods suggests their potential developmental toxicity and cardiotoxicity, i.e., most LCMs could alter body length, head area, eye area, heart rate, stroke volume, and area and volume of the ventricle during systole and diastole in zebrafish. Moreover, LCM-induced cardiotoxicity is closely associated with developmental defects, which represent manifestations of systemic toxicity-related responses rather than independent toxic endpoints. These findings provide important evidence for the hazard assessment of LCMs, and the methodology provides a powerful tool for high-throughput hazard screening and prioritization of emerging pollutants with developmental toxicity and cardiotoxicity.

title: Foliar CeO2 Nanoparticles Mitigate Cadmium Phytotoxicity in Strawberry by Suppressing Cd Accumulation and Activating a Secondary Metabolite Defense Network
abstract: Atmospheric cadmium (Cd) deposition threatens food safety, yet how beneficial nanoparticles (NPs) augment plant tolerance to heavy metal stress remains poorly understood. Here, we dissected the protective mechanisms of foliar-applied CeO2 NPs against Cd toxicity in strawberries by integrating physiology, transcriptomics, and metabolomics. Foliar Cd exposure caused significant Cd accumulation in leaves (9.77 mg/kg dry weight) and translocation to roots and fruits (0.964 and 0.292 mg/kg dry weight). This resulted in 70.5% inhibition of photosynthesis and 20.6% and 29.0% increases in MDA and GSH relative to those of the control, indicating photosynthetic damage and oxidative stress. Coapplied CeO2 NPs counteracted this phytotoxicity by reducing leaf Cd by 23.4% and lowering MDA contents by 16.8%, consequently restoring photosynthesis by 2.30-fold. Multiomics unveiled the molecular basis of this biostimulation. Specifically, CeO2 NPs upregulated gene expression involved in hormone signaling and terpenoid biosynthesis (e.g., EIN3, JAZ, MVD, and DXS) and levels of flavonoids, phenol ethers, and l-glutamate, which support the oxidative stress prevention and plant defense. Moreover, redox homeostasis, associated with these genes and metabolites alongside Cd accumulation, regulated photosynthesis (effect size: −0.604). This work suggests a mechanistic dual-action hypothesis and positions CeO2 NPs as a sustainable nanostrategy for safeguarding crops against atmospheric heavy metal stress.

title: Fe–N x -Coordinated Algal Carbon with CaS for Enhanced and Extended Dechlorination of Chlorinated Hydrocarbons by Zero-Valent Iron
abstract: Sulfidation improves the electron selectivity of zero-valent iron (ZVI), whereas Fe–Nx coordination structures could lower intrinsic dechlorination energy barriers. However, the synergistic integration of these two functionalities and their cooperative mechanism remain unclear. Here, we synthesized an algae-derived carbon material (Fex@NBC) containing both Fe–Nx sites and CaS via pyrolysis of iron-laden algal sludge. Upon coupling with nanoscale ZVI (nZVI), CaS-induced in situ sulfidation generated FeSx at the Fe0 surface, forming a dual-functional architecture with FeSx and Fe–Nx sites. The Fex@NBC/nZVI system achieved 84.3% of trichloroethylene (TCE) dechlorination within 24 h with a rate constant of 0.12 h–1 and an electron efficiency of 80.5%. Notably, 23.8% of the recalcitrant 1,2-dichloroethane (1,2-DCA) was degraded within 50 days, demonstrating an extended dechlorination boundary. Mechanistic investigations reveal that Fe–Nx sites serve as the primary catalytic centers, while FeSx enhances interfacial electron transfer from Fe0 to Fe–Nx and suppresses hydrogen evolution. The cooperative regulation of catalytic activation and electron utilization remains effective under aging, ion influence, and realistic groundwater conditions. This work provides a resource-recovery concept for valorizing iron-enriched algal sludge while revealing the cooperative mechanism between Fe–Nx catalysis and FeSx-mediated electron regulation in ZVI-based remediation systems.

title: Electron-Withdrawing Picolinate Substituents Accelerate Fe(III)/Fe(II) Cycling in Fenton Reactions
abstract: The Fe(III)/Fe(II) redox cycle is the driving force of Fenton chemistry, governing the generation of reactive oxidants, the efficiency of H2O2 utilization, and the amount of iron sludge. However, rational regulation of Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling remains a long-standing challenge, largely due to the poorly understood relationship between iron electronic structures and iron redox kinetics. Here, using the ferric picolinate complex (FeIII–PICA)-mediated Fenton reaction as a model system, we systematically investigate how the iron electronic structure influences Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling by varying the substituent group on PICA. Electron-withdrawing substituents markedly accelerate Fe(III) reduction, hydroxyl radical generation, and pollutant degradation. The kinetic analysis, combined with theoretical calculations, identifies Fe–O homolysis of the ferric hydroperoxo intermediate (PICA–FeIII–OOH) as the rate-limiting step of Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling. Electronic structure analysis reveals that electron-withdrawing substituents narrow the gap of redox-active orbitals of PICA–FeIII–OOH to lower the reaction barrier for Fe–O homolysis. Consequently, this orbital modulation facilitates electron transfer to the iron center and accelerates iron cycling. Furthermore, the energy level of the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (ELUMO) serves as a more accessible descriptor that quantitatively captures substituent effects across different substitution types and positions. These findings establish a quantitative structure–reactivity relationship for Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling of Fenton reactions, providing a preliminary design pattern for developing efficient iron-based catalysts.

title: Advancing a Circular Economy: A Special Issue in Environmental Science & Technology , ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering , and ACS Sustainable Resource Management
abstract: RecommendationsM odern economies have largely developed around a linear "take-make-use-dispose" model: extracting natural resources, transforming them into products, using those products, and discarding the resulting materials and residuals.Although this model has supported extraordinary advances in health, technology, and prosperity, it has also accelerated resource depletion, pollution, biodiversity loss, and climate change.It has created dependencies on geographically concentrated critical materials, with associated economic and geopolitical risks, while many of its environmental and social costs fall disproportionately on communities with the fewest resources to bear them.A circular economy offers a different vision, one in which products and processes are designed to retain the value of materials, carbon, water, and energy; waste streams become resources; and renewable feedstocks displace finite or environmentally consequential inputs.Realizing that vision, however, requires more than closing material loops.Circularity is not inherently sustainable: recycling, recovery, and reuse can require substantial energy and chemical inputs, create new emissions or routes of exposure, or shift burdens among locations and populations.Progress therefore depends on innovation coupled with rigorous science and engineering to move beyond simple circularity to achieve genuinely beneficial environmental, economic, and social outcomes.These considerations motivated the 2024-2025 open call for papers for the joint Special Issue "Advancing a Circular Economy".The resulting collection in Environmental Science & Technology, ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering, and ACS Sustainable Resource Management brings together more than 80 articles spanning the recovery of nutrients, critical minerals, metals, and other resources from wastewater, industrial residuals, mine tailings, coal ash, and electronic waste.The contributions investigate lithium, rare earth elements, platinum-group metals, silver, magnesium, gold, phosphorus, and other valuable resources using approaches that include selective separations, electrochemistry, leaching, precipitation, crystallization, and direct regeneration.Other studies examine circularity at broader product, supply chain, regional, and global scales by mapping stocks and flows of building materials, electronic waste, vanadium, photovoltaic waste, and other anthropogenic resources.Together, these articles demonstrate the importance of connecting advances in recovery technologies with a deeper understanding of resource availability, environmental implications, and the broader societal systems in which these technologies would operate.

title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
Nationwide Study of Per-and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Dragonfly Larvae and Water in United States Protected Areas
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widespread in the environment and are of global concern because of their prevalence, persistence, and toxicity. Information about PFAS on federally protected and Tribal lands is limited, despite calls from scientific and regulatory communities for data on environmental background concentrations. To respond to this, we leveraged an existing citizen-science network to collect dragonfly larvae (n = 179 sites) and water (n = 81 sites) from 108 national parks, national wildlife refuges, forests, and Tribal lands across the continental United States and Puerto Rico. Our results showed that PFAS are widespread, with PFOS and PFBA frequently observed (>60% of samples) in dragonfly larvae and water, respectively. Individual PFAS concentrations ranged from 0.22 to 56.6 ng/L in water and 0.10 to 480 ng/g dry weight in dragonfly larvae. Results from this novel broad-scale assessment indicated that concentrations were greater, and profiles were more diverse, in the eastern compared to western United States. Potential drivers of bioaccumulation were distance to source, habitat type, and land use, and large-scale variation in bioaccumulation was related to ecoregion and precipitation. Information from this study can help identify localized hotspots, prioritize monitoring and modeling efforts, and inform future management strategies.

title: Heatwaves Trigger Nonlinear Rises in Nonmethane Hydrocarbons
abstract: Urban heatwaves intensify ozone and particulate pollution by accelerating volatile organic compound (VOC) oxidation in the presence of nitrogen oxides (NOx). However, the temperature dependence of anthropogenic nonmethane hydrocarbons (NMHCs) remains poorly constrained and may become strongly nonlinear under extreme heat. The temperature response of anthropogenic VOC emissions depends on species-specific physicochemical properties. Here, we show that anthropogenic NMHC concentrations measured in Guangzhou, China, exhibit two distinct temperature thresholds at 26.5 °C (associated with the dew point) and near 30 °C (associated with an effective volatility threshold), above which concentrations increase abruptly. Using high-resolution observations, statistical classification, and thermodynamic simulations, we show that these thresholds arise from coupled volatility and chemical-reactivity effects that link phase behavior to atmospheric chemical loss. Chemical depletion accelerates with warming but exhibits diminishing marginal sensitivity, while ambient NMHCs volatilize in three hierarchical batches ordered by boiling point. These nonlinear concentration responses are not captured by traditional steady-state emission parametrizations that assume simple linear temperature scaling. Incorporating threshold-based volatilization behavior into urban chemistry models should improve predictions of ozone formation and particulate pollution during heatwaves and under future climate warming.

title: Redox Perturbations Promote Oxidative and Cometabolic Reaction Networks for Enhanced Organic Micropollutant Removal in Activated Sludge
Advanced Classification of Light-Absorbing Aerosols Using a Two-Dimensional Absorption Ångström Exponent (2D AAE) Space
abstract: Light-absorbing aerosols (LAA) play a critical role in climate forcing and remain one of the largest sources of uncertainty in climate models. Ambient aerosols exhibit complex absorption spectral features making the Absorption Ångström Exponent (AAE) calculation highly sensitive to the chosen wavelength range, which can significantly affect interpretations of aerosol properties and source contribution. This study introduces an advanced classification framework for LAA using multiwavelength absorption measurements and a two-dimensional AAE approach, strengthened by absorption deviation in UV (2D AAE + Δ340). For the first time, continuous field measurements at seven European sites using a new nine-wavelength Aethalometer (AE36s; 340–950 nm) were combined with targeted laboratory experiments to systematically characterize aerosol absorption properties. AAE was calculated over two spectral ranges, AAE400–590 (400, 470, 520, 590 nm) and AAE590–950 (590, 630, 880, 950 nm) and the relative deviation at 340 nm from the AAE400–590-derived power law fit (Δ340) was introduced as an additional metric. The resulting 2D AAE fingerprints enable robust discrimination among fresh and aged black carbon (BCfresh, BCaged), residential and open biomass-burning aerosol (BBres and BBopen), and mineral dust. The proposed 2D AAE approach significantly improves LAA type identification and source apportionment compared with conventional single-range AAE analysis, enhancing interpretation of multiwavelength absorption data and supporting more accurate assessment of aerosol climate and air-quality impacts.

title: Precipitation-Modulated Differential Scavenging of Atmospheric Nitric Acid, Nitrogen Dioxide, and Particulate Nitrate: Isotopic Constraints on Wet Nitrate Sources
abstract: Quantifying the relative contributions of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and gaseous nitric acid (HNO3), and particulate nitrate (p-NO3–) to wet NO3– (w-NO3–) and understanding their differential scavenging remain critical challenges for nitrogen deposition modeling. Traditional approaches often neglect direct NO2 scavenging, introducing source apportionment uncertainties. Here, we compile a global dual-isotope (δ15N, δ18O) data set covering w-NO3– and its three precursors across 91 sites in Asia, North America, and Europe. Using an isotope mass-balance model, we quantify fractional contributions (F values) and preferential scavenging degrees (β values) of each precursor and examine their responses to mean annual precipitation. Average F values for NO2, HNO3, and p-NO3– are 26 ± 18, 39 ± 20, and 35 ± 20%, respectively, while their atmospheric abundance fractions (f values) are 76 ± 12, 9 ± 7, and 15 ± 11%. β values follow a universal order (βHNO3 > βp-NO3– > βNO2), confirming that HNO3 is preferentially scavenged. Precipitation modulates β values species-specifically: βHNO3 decreases with increasing precipitation, whereas βNO2 increases. Notably, our results suggest a tentative shift toward p-NO3– as the dominant precursor of w-NO3– at roughly 1750 mm of mean annual precipitation, although this crossing does not represent a statistically robust threshold. These findings provide quantitative constraints for model parametrization and inform region-specific nitrogen mitigation strategies.

title: A Chain of Multiple Cryptic N-Fe-Mn-CH4 Redox Couplings in Methanogenic Lake Sediments
abstract: Approximately 30% of methane (CH4) emissions originate from freshwater sediments, typically oxygen- and sulfate (SO42-)-depleted, limiting their ability to regulate CH4 release. Here, we unravel a chain of triple cryptic N-Mn/Fe-CH4 redox couplings in natural, unpolluted reduced methanogenic lake sediments, which impact their cycles while sustaining complex aerobic and anaerobic microbial communities. Sediment profiles revealed an unexpected increase in nitrite (NO2-) along with elevated Fe2+, Mn2+, active NC10 bacteria, and aerobic methanotrophs and decreased CH4 levels. Sediment incubations amended under anoxic conditions with labeled ammonium (15NH4+) produced 15NO2- and 15N2, indicating anaerobic NH4+ oxidation, likely coupled to Mn(IV)/Fe(III) reduction. We further identified a sink for NO3-/NO2- coupled to Fe2+ oxidation, with Fe2+ partly derived from Fe(III)-dependent CH4 oxidation. The activity of NC10 bacteria and Methylococcales suggests an additional NO2- sink via NO2- disproportionation and potentially dark oxygen production, thereby facilitating aerobic CH4 oxidation under anoxic conditions. These coupled cycles likely dominate sulfate-depleted, organic- and Mn/Fe-rich methanogenic freshwater sediments, including many eutrophic lakes and wetlands that are expected to expand under global warming.

title: Humic and Fulvic Acids Elicit Distinct Multi-Organ and Microbial Responses after Chronic Oral Exposure
abstract: Humic acid (HA) and fulvic acid (FA) are major constituents of natural organic matter (NOM) that can exhibit dynamic supramolecular and colloidal organization in aqueous environments. Given the widespread occurrence of NOM in environmental waters and that untreated natural water can represent a chronic oral exposure source for wildlife and populations lacking safely managed drinking water, the intrinsic biological effects of HA and FA after chronic oral exposure remain insufficiently understood. Here, we conducted a 90-day multidose oral mouse exposure integrating histopathology, biochemistry, gut microbiome profiling, and untargeted metabolomics to evaluate responses to Suwannee River humic acid (SRHA) and fulvic acid (SRFA). Both substances were associated with lipid-related metabolic alterations, intestinal mucosal changes, neural alterations, and oxidative-stress-related responses. SRHA, with higher aromaticity and apparent molecular weight, showed broader gut microbial changes, whereas SRFA, with lower apparent molecular weight and higher polarity, showed broader metabolic alterations in serum, liver, and brain. Multiomics integration revealed distinct microbiota–metabolome associations, while complementary interface assays suggested that structural and interfacial differences may contribute to these response patterns. These findings demonstrate distinct biological responses to chronic SRHA and SRFA exposure, supporting further consideration of the intrinsic bioactivity of humic substances in environmental exposure assessment.

title: Rapid Conversion of Criegee-Derived Organic Peroxides into Distinct Organic Nitrogen Products via Interfacial Reaction with Amines
abstract: Organic nitrogen (ON) compounds represent a substantial fraction of atmospheric reactive nitrogen, yet the mechanisms governing their secondary formation in the condensed phase remain poorly constrained. In this study, we investigated the interfacial reactions between terpenoid-derived organic peroxides (OPs), specifically α-acyloxyalkyl-hydroperoxides (α-AAHs) and α-alkoxyalkyl-hydroperoxides (α-AHs), with common atmospheric amines (ethylamine, dimethylamine, and propylamine) using surface-sensitive mass spectrometry and isotope labeling. Our results demonstrate that α-AAHs react rapidly with amines to form ON products via a nucleophilic addition–elimination mechanism, sharing a common pathway with α-hydroxyalkyl-hydroperoxides (α-HHs). Notably, α-AAHs exhibit even faster kinetics than α-HHs, with calculated atmospheric half-lives (τ1/2) as short as subminute at 10 ppt amine exposure. In contrast, α-AHs show relatively inert toward amines compared to α-AAHs, and their reactions with ethylamine and dimethylamine proceed via distinct formation pathways. Kinetic analysis reveals that these interfacial interactions are reaction-limited processes, unaffected by variations in interfacial solvent structure. These findings identify direct reactions of Criegee-derived OPs with amines as a potentially rapid pathway to ON formation that may complement conventional carbonyl–amine chemistry. This study highlights a previously underestimated non-negligible source of secondary organic nitrogen, which is essential for accurately assessing aerosol impacts on air quality, human health, and climate forcing.

title: Resilient Net Community Production in a Warming North Pacific Ocean (2001–2019)
abstract: Net community production (NCP)─carbon fixation remaining after autotrophic and heterotrophic respiration─regulates surface fCO2, air–sea CO2 exchange, and the ocean’s vertical carbon gradient. However, sparse measurements limit our understanding of its long-term variability at basin scales. We estimated North Pacific NCP at 1° × 1° resolution for 2001–2019 from the warming-period (wp) drawdown of dissolved inorganic carbon (CT) in the surface mixed layer. CT was reconstructed from more than 3.3 million surface fCO2 observations and empirically estimated total alkalinity using carbonate-system thermodynamics, with corrections for salinity, net air–sea CO2 exchange, vertical diffusion, and CaCO3 production. Mean NCP was 1.3 ± 0.1 Pg C wp–1 and exhibited no long-term trend despite 0.6 °C of basin-wide warming, which is expected to suppress biological production by strengthening stratification and limiting nutrient supply. This apparent stability masked opposing trends: declining NCP in the western deep-mixed-layer region was offset by increasing NCP in the tropics, potentially supported by enhanced nitrogen fixation. Thus, basin-wide stability reflected regional compensation rather than a uniform response to warming. Nevertheless, a projected NCP decline of approximately 0.16 Pg C yr–1 by 2100 is equivalent in magnitude to approximately 30% of the basin’s current net air–sea CO2 uptake.

Data-driven master planning of a circular plastic recycling supply chain: A case study
abstract: The growing accumulation of plastic waste and the complexity of reverse logistics planning make circular plastic recycling a critical yet challenging task. To address this issue, this paper proposes a data-driven master planning framework for the circular Plastic Recycling Supply Chain (PRSC), integrating forward and reverse logistics decisions into a unified model. The proposed multi-period Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model considers multiple product characteristics, such as type and color, as well as customer clustering based on demand behavior and strategic importance. Additionally, it accounts for the recovery of plastic waste from both post-industrial and partial post-consumer sources. However, existing studies have paid limited attention to the consideration of customer heterogeneity, differentiated waste-return behavior, multi-period returned-waste inventory management, and material conversion processes within a plastic recycling supply chain optimization framework. A case study of a recycling company is used to validate the model. The model is solved using CPLEX and two meta-heuristic algorithms, namely Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), to evaluate optimality and computational performance. Results show that enabling customer returns decreases total system costs by about 6% compared with a non-return scenario, while reducing purchase costs by nearly 30% and increasing transportation and recycling costs by around 5%. Overall, the proposed framework offers a practical decision-support tool that enhances circularity and resource efficiency across the plastic supply chain.

Consumer sickness behavior: A model for understanding consumption during illness
abstract: Illness is a near‐universal and economically consequential consumer state, yet consumer theory has no framework for how being sick changes consumption. Prior work has focused on external pandemic responses and not the internal biological state of being sick, and little research connects the biological mechanisms of illness (inflammation, cytokine activation) to systematic change in consumer behavior. Drawing on converging evidence from immunology, neuroscience, and consumer behavior, we develop the Consumer Sickness Behavior (CSB) model. The model proposes that illness activates an adaptive motivational program with three psychological mediators: motivational reprioritization, risk‐perception recalibration, and effort‐value recalibration. It predicts a distinctive differential‐effects pattern, the simultaneous suppression of exploratory and social consumption and amplification of comfort‐ and safety‐seeking, that neither a single feeling state nor fatigue produces. By treating illness as a compound psychological state, in which acute inflammation produces feelings and motivational changes together, CSB explains marketplace patterns that no account based on a single feeling or on fatigue predicts and offers implications for marketing, consumer welfare, and public health.

title: Excessive Heat and Correctional Officer Turnover: Evidence From Texas
abstract: Correctional work is difficult, dangerous, and hot. Many US prisons lack air‐conditioning, resulting in sweltering conditions for both incarcerated people and the street‐level bureaucrats tasked with their supervision. We examine the effect of working in the summer heat without air‐conditioning on correctional officer turnover using personnel records of nearly 60,000 Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ) employees across 68 prisons between 2010 and 2023. We demonstrate that, among the least‐experienced frontline employees before the onset of COVID‐19, the difference in the probability of departing between those working in prisons without and with air‐conditioning is, on average, 0.33 percentage points larger in the hottest months than in the coolest—an approximately 12% change relative to the baseline departure rate. Back‐of‐the‐envelope estimates suggest that installing air‐conditioning to combat understaffing is comparable in cost to raising salaries, the TDCJ's standard response to high turnover.

title: Engineering Co/CoO heterophase interfaces on carbonized polyaniline for Co(IV)=O-dominated PMS activation

Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome
abstract: Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment 1,2. How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour–stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

title: Dual proofs of legendary Riemann hypothesis stun mathematicians
Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
abstract: Molecular and morphological evidence increasingly supports the view that most East Asian Middle to Late Pleistocene archaic Homo belong to Denisovans 1 , yet the presence of other contemporaneous lineages has remained unclear. Here we report a set of newly discovered hominin fossils (4 isolated teeth; more than 100.8 thousand years ago and 104.5–42.6 thousand years ago, respectively) from 2 cave sites (Chuanshandong and Longchuandong) in Guangxi, southern China. Integrated morphological and palaeoproteomic analyses reveal substantial phenotypic and molecular diversity consistent with at least two distinct lineages. One lineage (Longchuandong) is assigned to a Denisovan-affinity population, owing to its extreme similarity to Altai Denisovans with respect to dental morphology and single amino acid polymorphisms that match those of Denisovans from Harbin, Penghu, Bianfu Cave and Altai. The other lineage, represented by the Chuanshandong hominin, is an unresolved archaic Homo , as it carries an ancestral variant (AMELY 179M) shared with Homo antecessor and great apes and another variant (AMBN 253G) that is diagnostic of East Asian Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus but lacks the Denisovan-associated AMBN 273V variant (it being highly probable that this is inherited from H. erectus ). Dental morphology in this lineage exhibits a mosaic of plesiomorphic and derived traits but no clear Denisovan affinity. These findings indicate that diverse hominin populations may have inhabited subtropical China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene, including a Denisovan-affinity population and another unresolved archaic Homo .

title: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP
Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis
An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells
Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids
abstract: Colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges 1 . Here we demonstrate a spin-exchange-driven phototransport regime in manganese-doped quantum dot films that enables the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers. Ultrafast spin-exchange-mediated Auger upconversion promotes electrons into high-energy, delocalized states before phonon cooling 2 , 3 , establishing a transient high-mobility conduction channel. Crucially, spin-exchange interactions not only generate hot carriers but also enable their repeated re-excitation, thereby sustaining long-range drift. This mechanism yields room-temperature mobilities of about 150 cm 2 V −1 s −1 and submillimetre drift lengths—far greater than those of conventional quantum dot solids and approaching values characteristic of crystalline semiconductors. Time-of-flight measurements confirm drift-dominated transport, with transit times scaling linearly with distance and inversely with electric field. These results establish a route to long-range energy transport in nanoscale materials and enable the use of hot carriers in photoconversion, photochemistry and transit-time-limited photodetection.

title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
abstract: Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering. CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) 1 , 2 offer a promising solution by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration. Because of their exceptional targeting fidelity, type I-F3 CASTs have been a major research focus 1 , yet the structural basis of their RNA-guided DNA integration has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, computational protein design and functional assays, we report the licensing mechanisms that control DNA integration activity of Vibrio cholerae CAST (VchCAST). Structural determination was enabled by zero-shot computational redesign of TnsA, which enhanced integration activity by nearly two orders of magnitude without compromising specificity. The structure of the holo integration complex reveals the conformational licensing events that govern activation of the integration machinery at the on-target site. Multiple components (Cascade–TniQ, TnsC and TnsA–TnsB) undergo conformational changes upon assembly into the holo integration complex, and the catalytically competent state is stabilized only within the full assembly. Comparison with existing CAST integration complex structures reveals conserved architectural features, suggesting a common molecular basis for RNA-guided transposition across CASTs. Our findings establish a general mechanistic framework for RNA-guided DNA integration and demonstrate that protein design is a powerful strategy for engineering highly active CAST systems.

title: Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing
An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals
abstract: Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production 1 , 2 . On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30–40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions 3 , 4 . As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate 5 . Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress 6 . Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ , a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4–32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7–42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

title: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
abstract: CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR–Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex 1,2. Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools 3–6. Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST (Pse CAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far 7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution 8. However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation 9. Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the Pse CAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the Pse CAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade–TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa Pse CAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC–TnsB and TnsB–target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

title: A gut–brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila
Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro
Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics 1 , 2 . Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively 2 , rare variation remains relatively unexplored 1 . Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency < 0.0001%) putative loss-of-function variants, implicated 17 genes with large effects on height ranging from −17cm ( ACAN ) to +11 cm ( FBN1 ) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes ( TET1 , DTL and IGF2BP2 ) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects—often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes—and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization.

title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts
abstract: Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide 1–4, yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999–2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species’ elevational ranges: upper portions of species’ ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease
abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease 1 , 2 . Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling 3 , we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956 -mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb–seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation
abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features.

title: Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons
Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
abstract: Heterochromatin typically represses genes 1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation 3–7. How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent 8. In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly 8. By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

title: What is the Riemann hypothesis? A guide to the famed conjecture that rules prime numbers
Saving Nepal’s wild orchids — in photos
Bogong moths can migrate using an internal geomagnetic compass
abstract: Australian migratory moths navigate long distances, in part owing to a stellar ‘compass’. It transpires that they have another compass that detects the inclination, or angle, of Earth’s magnetic field lines and that probably relies on a light-dependent quantum-mechanical mechanism similar to the one found in night-migratory songbirds. Migratory moths distinguish poleward from equatorward by sensing the inclination of magnetic field lines.

title: How arteries keep their shape in the face of overgrowth-inducing mutations
Pockets in compacted DNA tune gene activation
Enzymatic reactions adapted to make ‘living’ chains of sugars
A fine-grained reconstruction of barley’s evolutionary history
abstract: Chromosome-scale genome sequences from across the barley genus Hordeum reveal large structural variation, evidence of ancient genetic exchange and extensive divergence of regulatory sequences. These evolutionary processes have generated diversity that could be used to improve cultivated barley. Genome sequences across Hordeum reveal conserved chromosome ends and coding genes, but divergent chromosome centres and regulatory DNA.

The Labor Demand and Labor Supply Channels of Monetary Policy
abstract: Monetary policy is typically understood to affect employment through labor demand, with the role of labor supply receiving less consideration. We estimate the response of labor market flows to high-frequency changes in interest rates around FOMC announcements and Fed Chair speeches, and find that a contractionary monetary policy shock leads to a significant increase in labor supply: workers reduce the rate at which they quit jobs to nonemployment, and non-employed individuals increase their job-seeking behavior. These effects are quantitatively important: holding supply-driven labor market flows constant, the decline in employment from a contractionary monetary policy shock would be twice as large. To interpret our findings, we estimate a heterogeneous agent model with frictional labor markets and an active extensive margin of labor supply. The model rationalizes existing estimates of modest labor supply responses to idiosyncratic transfers with our new evidence of a large labor supply response to an aggregate shock.

title: Fine Stratification of Survey Experiments
abstract: This paper studies a two-stage model of experimentation, where the researcher first samples representative experimental participants from an eligible pool, then assigns each sampled unit to treatment or control, using matched k-tuples randomization at both stages. To implement such designs, we develop a fast algorithm for matching units into k-tuples for any k ≥ 2 and any dimension of covariates. By surveying 200 recent experimental working papers, we estimate that our algorithm newly enables multivariate fine stratification with provable match quality guarantees in about 48% of recent papers. We show that finely stratified sampling and assignment both nonparametrically reduce the variance of treatment effect estimation, with the gains from stratified sampling increasing in the size of the eligible pool and how well covariates predict treatment effect heterogeneity. We develop new inference methods that fully exploit the efficiency gains from both design stages, allowing researchers to report smaller standard errors if they designed a representative experiment. An application to nine published experiments quantifies the efficiency gains.

title: International Power
abstract: An interconnected world increases economic efficiency while giving certain countries leverage over others. We aim to describe and understand international power stemming from trade. Using an illustrative model of trade with possibilities of bilateral disputes and ex-post hold-ups, we highlight that bilateral asymmetry in import dependence can be a source of power towards one another. We construct the model-implied measure of international power — asymmetric bilateral import dependence, weighted inversely by sectoral trade elasticities — across country pairs over the past 20 years. Combining this measure with comprehensive data on bilateral engagement events and a high-frequency measure of bilateral geopolitical relationships, we examine the consequences and strategic causes of international power. We present two main empirical results. First, increases in international power between countries — which raise the credibility of threats of trade disruptions — induce more bilateral engagement and negotiations. Second, evidence suggests that worsened geopolitical relationships — in anticipation of future disputes — prompt countries to build up greater international power through adjusting trade activities.

Climate–Agrifood–Conflict Nexus Pathways: A Scoping Review of the Literature
abstract: This paper reviews how climate-related shocks influence conflict through the agrifood system. Drawing on a scoping review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2014 and 2024, it shows that the climate–agrifood–conflict nexus is indirect, context-specific and shaped mainly by two pathways: competition over natural resources and changes in agricultural productivity. The literature points to a positive association of higher temperatures and drought with conflict, whereas precipitation effects vary in sign, and to heterogeneity across conflict type, crop-calendar phases and institutional settings. The paper concludes by discussing the distinction between mediators and moderators, scarcity versus abundance and priorities for more mechanism-oriented research.

title: How Cost-Effective Were Subsidies for Solar Energy in Germany?
abstract: We study Germany’s photovoltaic subsidy program, estimating a dynamic model of new technology adoption which accounts for heterogeneity in residential ownership structures. We find that homeowner and landlord investors heavily discount future benefits, highlighting the suboptimality of the feed-in tariff structure and the inefficient use of government funds. Our estimates suggest that administrative costs associated with tenant electricity contracts discourage landlords from investing in new energy technologies. Our analysis suggests that policy design should prioritize upfront investment subsidies over feed-in tariffs to promote renewable energy adoption. Reducing administrative costs associated with tenant electricity programs is key to unlock investments by landlords and expand tenants’ access to solar energy, thereby enhancing cost-effectiveness.

title: Compulsory education and occupational persistence in US agriculture
Does High‐Speed Internet Access Affect the Mental Health of Older Adults?
abstract: Recent evidence finds a negative effect of the internet on younger people's mental health, but less is known about older adults, who are more vulnerable to both mental health issues and online deception. This study estimates the effect of broadband expansion on the mental health of older adults in the United States. Using individual panel data, a staggered broadband rollout, and the latest difference‐in‐differences methods, I find broadband significantly improves older adults' mental health, reducing depression symptoms by 5.7% and clinical symptoms of depression by 10%. Potential mechanisms include an increase in the self‐use of the internet, declines in feelings of social isolation and loneliness and suggestive evidence of improvements in the quality of virtual social connections. I find no evidence of other potential mechanisms, such as medication use for anxiety or depression and labor force outcomes, providing further support for the social mechanisms. Heterogeneity analyses provide evidence of larger improvements among rural residents, women, White respondents, and married respondents, with the clearest difference between rural and urban respondents. This work highlights broadband's additional unmeasured benefits to public investments, given the allocation of over 65 billion to broadband expansion in recent years.

title: Household-Level Responses to the European Energy Crisis
abstract: Cost-of-living shocks can have large and unequal effects, but causal evidence on households' adaptive responses is scarce. Using Finnish administrative microdata from the 2022 energy crisis, we exploit variation in electricity contract expirations to identify behavioral responses in electricity use, labor earnings, financial distress, and residual consumption and savings. We find notable heterogeneity in responses that shape the final incidence: High-income households primarily reduced electricity consumption, while low-income households reduced consumption less, responding instead through increased labor supply, more payment defaults, and cutbacks in spending and savings. Longer anticipation softens but does not eliminate these impacts. (JEL D12, D91, G51, J22, J31, L94, Q41)

title: Measuring Sensitive Outcomes through Ballot Bag Surveys
abstract: Prevailing methods for measuring sensitive outcomes confront researchers with an inherent bias-variance trade-off: Direct questioning is prone to a sensitivity bias, while indirect methods such as list experiments are substantially less precise. We test the ballot bag, a novel technique that relaxes this trade-off by mitigating bias in direct questioning while improving precision over indirect methods. In an experiment in Egypt, where direct questions on irregular migration are biased, ballot bag estimates are not statistically different from a list experiment but exhibit lower variance. Consequently, treatment effects are highly significant via the ballot bag and not via the list experiment. (JEL C83, C93, E24, J61, K37, L25, O15)

title: The Missing Poor
abstract: Population censuses constitute the basis of public resource allocation and political representation. This paper shows that census forms commonly generate incentives for enumerators to disproportionately omit members of larger households. Using microdata from 254 censuses, we estimate that this leads to undercounting in at least 60 percent of censuses. Omission is concentrated in poor countries where 0.6 percent of the population is missing. Within countries, poor households are missing three times as many members as rich ones, leading to larger undercounts in poorer regions. We illustrate how this translates into underfunding of public services and political underrepresentation in poor regions. (JEL C81, D72, I32, J11, O12)

title: Bonus Question: How Does Flexible Incentive Pay Affect Unemployment Dynamics?
abstract: We introduce dynamic incentive contracts into a model of unemployment fluctuations. Our main result is that wage cyclicality from incentives does not affect the response of unemployment to productivity shocks. The response of unemployment is the same, to a first order, in two economies: one with flexible incentive pay and another with exogenously fixed wages. This equivalence is due to movements in effort. Under the optimal incentive contract, firms' profits do not change when wages fall because the effort of the worker falls too. (JEL E24, J24, J31, J41, J63, J64, L25)

title: Rules versus Discretion without Common Knowledge
abstract: This paper revisits the classical time-inconsistent problem à la Barro and Gordon (1983) while relaxing the common knowledge assumption. When information is complete, achieving the first-best outcome is not possible, and the welfare under committed rules surpasses that under discretion. In contrast, without common knowledge, a policymaker adhering to committed rules can always attain the first-best outcome. If a commitment device is unavailable, the resulting welfare loss can either increase or decrease relative to the common knowledge benchmark. (JEL D83, E60)

title: Public Debt Levels and Real Interest Rates: Causal Evidence from Parliamentary Elections
abstract: We use close parliamentary elections as natural experiments to estimate the debt sensitivity of interest rates. Relative to an election in which one party barely secures a majority, an election in which no party achieves a majority causes the debt-to-GDP ratio to increase by 17 percentage points, while real interest rates rise by 99 basis points. If elections only impact real rates via debt, our results imply that a 1 percentage point increase in the debt-to-GDP ratio causes a 5.8 basis point increase in real rates, larger than most previous estimates. (JEL D72, E23, E43, E62, H63)

title: Cool Cities: The Value of Urban Trees
abstract: As urban populations grow, more people face extreme heat, increasing demand for natural cooling. Urban trees offer various amenities, including cooling benefits, yet their economic value is hard to quantify. This paper estimates the implicit value of urban trees by exploiting the emerald ash borer infestation of ash trees in Toronto as an exogenous shock. We find that a 1 percentage point increase in a postcode's tree cover raises property prices by 1.13 percent and reduces exposure to extreme heat, pollution, and energy consumption. These findings underscore trees as a cost-effective, practical strategy for mitigating urban warming. (JEL Q23, Q41, Q53, Q54, Q58, R11, R53)

title: The Lasting Effects of Working While in School: A Long-Term Follow-Up
abstract: This paper provides the first experimental evidence on the long-term effects of work-study programs, leveraging a randomized lottery design from a national program in Uruguay. Participation leads to a persistent 11 percent increase in formal labor earnings seven years after the program, driven by a 4 percent increase in the monthly probability of being employed and a 6 percent increase in monthly wages. Effects are significantly larger for men, while remaining positive for women. The program is highly cost-effective, outperforming most job training programs and reaching levels comparable to early-childhood investments. (JEL D44, I21, I26, J13, J24, J31, O15)

title: Ten Years of Relational Power: The Long-Run Effects of Teaching Negotiation Skills to Adolescent Girls
abstract: We evaluate the effects of teaching negotiation skills to adolescent girls in economically vulnerable communities in Lusaka, Zambia, ten years later. Treated participants complete 0.23 more years of education. Consistent with greater relational empowerment, they also begin sexual activity later, have smaller age gaps with their husbands, and express less traditional gender attitudes. Using a surrogate approach, social benefits and costs from increased education alone suggest that the intervention generated 7.6 dollars for every dollar spent and had a very high marginal value of public funds of 10.5. (JEL I12, I21, I26, J13, J16, J24, O15)

title: Breaking Gender Norms: A Dynamic Perspective on Entering Gender-Atypical Occupations
abstract: Occupational gender segregation remains a defining feature of labor markets worldwide, and efforts to recruit individuals into gender-atypical occupations often fail because newcomers drop out shortly after entry. Understanding what drives this early attrition requires examining the day-to-day experiences of newcomers whose gender is underrepresented in their occupation, especially during the critical first weeks of organizational socialization. Integrating role congruity theory with a dynamic work-events perspective, we propose that gender-atypical newcomers experience an intensifying trajectory of perceived negative work events over time, and that this intensifying trajectory undermines their task mastery and heightens their turnover intention. Results from a longitudinal field study applying a repeated-measures design to 673 newcomers across 88 occupations over 12 weeks support these predictions. Newcomers working in gender-atypical occupations experienced a significant increase in negative work events over time, with this effect being significantly stronger for men in female-dominated occupations than for women in male-dominated occupations. Furthermore, steeper negative work event trajectories were associated with lower task mastery and higher turnover intentions. These findings advance dissimilarity research by uncovering the dynamic mechanism through which gender dissimilarity translates into adverse adjustment outcomes and contribute to the anchoring events literature by demonstrating the disproportionate and lasting influence of early negative experiences at the very outset of a professional career.

title: Scalable Just-in-Time Price Elasticity Estimation
abstract: This paper presents a scalable, nonparametric approach to estimating point-wise price elasticities designed for real-time pricing decisions. A key challenge in these settings is correcting for price endogeneity while remaining computationally efficient. We address this by leveraging nonparametric control functions to decompose the identification of causal elasticities into a sequence of scalable intermediate prediction tasks. We implement this framework with bootstrap averaged (bagged) nearest neighbors, which admits a closed-form representation that enables scalable, real-time implementation. We establish uniform consistency of our estimator and show in Monte Carlo simulations that it robustly recovers local elasticities across a diverse range of data-generating processes. We demonstrate the method’s practical usefulness by applying it to the New York City ride-sharing market, recovering substantial spatial-temporal heterogeneity in price elasticity and updating citywide elasticity estimates in less than one minute, which provide a “just-in-time” input for algorithmic pricing systems. This paper was accepted by Raphael Thomadsen, marketing. Funding: J. Wang acknowledges financial support from the Research Grants Council of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China [Grant 14508924]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.04791 .

title: When GenAI Increases Inequality: Evidence from a University Debating Competition
abstract: Research on Generative AI (GenAI) and work reports both productivity-compressing and inequality-expanding effects, leaving open a central question for organizations: Who benefits from GenAI and on which specific tasks? I address this question through a randomized controlled trial in competitive university debating, where participants are randomly assigned access to GenAI. Although most previous experimental work examines the impact of GenAI on written activities and across individuals, this setting allows me to study the impact of GenAI on a knowledge-intensive spoken activity and to identify heterogeneous effects across subtasks. I find that GenAI expands performance inequality in this setting. Consistent with recent theories on GenAI and work, results show that high-ability participants experience significantly larger gains from GenAI usage than their lower-ability counterparts in judgment-intensive subtasks, whereas lower-ability individuals only improve their performance in less expert components of debating, where GenAI can be used as a substitute. If these inequality-expanding effects generalize to similar spoken settings where complex ideas must be internalized and explained, rather than simply written, they would have important implications for understanding the impact of GenAI on work and inequality. This paper was accepted by Maria Guadalupe, business strategy. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.01063 .

title: Machine Learning Vast Dynamic Conditional Covariance Matrices: The Spirit of “Divide and Conquer”
abstract: Large-scale portfolio selection requires accurate forecasts of high-dimensional dynamic conditional covariance matrices (CCMs). This task is challenging because the number of covariance elements grows quickly with the number of assets, whereas the available time-series observations are limited and noisy. In this paper, we propose a novel graph-based quantiled (GRAND) CCM estimator in the spirit of “divide and conquer.” By extracting information from the extensive asset features, the GRAND method leverages a new graph-based deep learning network, called the self-grouping autoencoder (SGA), to learn the conditional quantiles of returns. Using those learned conditional quantiles, the GRAND method further learns (co)variances of CCM element-wisely via the quantiled conditional moment (QCM) method, and finally, it makes the resulting assembled CCM estimator positive semidefinite through a projection. Because of the use of the SGA network and the QCM method in an element-wise way, the GRAND method is blessing dimensionality in learning the CCM of a large-scale portfolio, while keeping the computation manageable and maintaining causal semantics. From an extensive empirical analysis of the Chinese stock market, we show that the GRAND method can produce much better tangency portfolios than its competitors, and provide dynamic causal graphs to study variance and quantile connectedness of all stocks for interpreting systemic risk and forecasting the business cycle. This paper was accepted by Kay Giesecke, finance. Funding: This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72503203 and 72573142]; the Natural Science Foundation of Fujian Province [Grants 2025J01036 and 2025J08009]; the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities [Grant 20720251053]; and the Research Grants Council, University Grants Committee [Grants 17302424, 17304421, 17304723, and 17312622]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.08930 .

title: Online Job Selection: Reward Rate vs. Remaining Value
abstract: High-throughput systems, such as cloud spot markets, adaptive large language model inference, and order consolidation in logistics, operate under capacity constraints. In these settings, decision makers must allocate fixed resources among a stream of requests with heterogeneous reward rates and service durations. A critical tension arises when capacity is saturated; the system must decide whether to continue serving an active job to harvest its remaining value or to preempt it in favor of a new arrival. This trade-off is especially subtle when a new job offers a lower immediate reward rate but a longer service duration, potentially outweighing a high-rate job near completion. To address this challenge, we introduce a general and parsimonious online allocation framework for capacity-constrained resources, where preemption is nonresumable and yields partial rewards. This abstraction captures the essential dynamics of modern resource management problems, including but not limited to those discussed earlier. We derive intuitive index-based policies and provide constant-factor competitive-ratio guarantees for their performance without requiring any forecasts of future demand. In particular, we show that two naive index-based policies have competitive ratios of 1/2 and [Formula: see text]. Our main methodological contribution is to develop a flexible framework for defining “quasiutilities” that couples the states of an online algorithm versus an offline algorithm, which reduces the design of online index-based policies to an offline geometrical problem. The framework allows us to optimize the index function, leading to an exponential-index-based policy that has an improved competitive ratio of 0.68. We also consider various extensions and prove that most of our analyses are tight. Finally, we conduct a concise numerical study to demonstrate the strong empirical performance of the proposed policies under nonworst-case stochastic demand sequences. This paper was accepted by Jeannette Song, operations management. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.09109 .

title: The Effects of Search Interface on Consumer Preferences: Evidence from a Randomized Experiment
abstract: A randomized experiment shows how restricting search filters broadens product exposure, reshapes revealed attribute preferences, and increases choice diversity.

title: The reversal of gender disparities in the retention and promotion of Big Four auditors
abstract: Popular media and academic research have long characterized the Big Four audit firms as boys’ clubs that fail to equitably retain and promote women. Using data on more than 150,000 rank-and-file auditors, we show that women did face significantly lower rates of retention and promotion throughout the 1990s and 2000s. These disparities reversed during the mid-2010s, however, and female auditors now enjoy higher rates of retention and promotion than their male colleagues. We examine three drivers: increasing female representation on client audit committees, growing client emphasis on diversity in hiring and vendor selection, and the introduction of Form AP, which made lead audit partner identities public for the first time. Only Form AP significantly predicts the reversal when controlling for the other two. Consistent with Form AP’s salience, the reversal is absent among professionals with no Form AP exposure, muted where exposure is partial, and delayed in Big Four tax practices.

title: Inclusion at the periphery? On the targeted lacunae of neoliberal business schools and the epistemic anchoring of “Included” marginalized knowers
abstract: In this essay, I argue that the inclusion of marginalized knowers at the periphery of neoliberal business schools may be as pernicious as their exclusion. I show that epistemic marginalization persists because the forms of knowledge marginalized knowers seek to produce are situated within targeted lacunae, systematically produced, and actively maintained absences around particular bodies of knowledge. These lacunae constitute forbidden domains shaped by the normative structure of business schools and the interests of their powerful allies. Through this conceptualization, I argue that the margin is not an inferior outside to the center, but a structured absence constituted within it, necessary for the coherence and dominance of the center. In doing so, I challenge assumptions that meaningful dialogue between margin and center remains viable when the terms of engagement are already predetermined by the center itself. At the same time, through what I conceptualize as epistemic anchoring, I show that the persistence of marginalized bodies of knowledge depends not only, or even primarily, on engagement with the center, but on the construction and sustenance of alternative epistemic spaces and the ability of marginalized knowers to remain anchored within them.

title: Interaction zones theory: How social proximity emerges and shapes thriving at work
abstract: The rising digitalization of work risks eroding social proximity and the relational conditions that enable thriving through work. Against this background, we review literature on social proximity and identify a lack of theory explaining how feelings of interpersonal closeness emerge through social interactions at work. To address this gap, we develop interaction zones theory. We propose that the “social proximity zone” represents the intersection of two latent dimensions that we refer to as relational stakes and interactional ease, respectively. We use this two-by-two framework to characterize interactional experiences, building on the circumplex model of affect as a foundation. A central proposition is that repeated and shared interactions in the social proximity zone contribute to individual and team thriving, based on the assumption that thriving requires interactions that are sufficiently challenging to enable learning yet flow with sufficient ease to ensure vitality. Finally, we argue that the social proximity zone can be purposively designed by creating relational stakes (e.g., through individual job design) and facilitating interactional ease (e.g., through team design). We outline a multilevel research agenda, calling for renewed attention to the importance of human-to-human interaction for individual thriving, team effectiveness, and broader organizational capabilities.

title: Corporate Energy Performance: Energy Intensity, Renewable Energy and Sectoral Differences Among CAC 40 Companies
abstract: Corporate energy performance is difficult to compare across firms because energy use varies with economic scale and sectoral characteristics. This study examines CAC 40 companies during 2016–2020 using the proposed Environmental Performance Measurement Framework (EPMF). Total energy consumption is normalised by revenue and benchmarked within sector‐year peer groups; renewable‐energy share is assessed separately. The findings indicate reductions in energy intensity among many firms and increased renewable‐energy use where comparable data are available, while substantial differences persist within sectors. Sensitivity analyses also highlight the influence of benchmarking choices and sector classification on some scores. The analysis is descriptive and historical: It does not establish causal effects or directly measure strategic capabilities. By distinguishing energy intensity from renewable‐energy adoption and absolute changes from relative rankings, the study illustrates the potential and limitations of sector‐relative benchmarking for corporate environmental performance assessment.

title: A Sustainability Perspective on Industry 4.0 Technology: A Strategic Framework for Balanced Corporate Decision‐Making
abstract: Existing frameworks, such as life cycle assessment (LCA), are often underutilized by practitioners due to their complexity, limited context‐specific adaptation, and high resource demands. This study examines how sustainability beyond mere financial metrics can be integrated into corporate innovation decisions while addressing these barriers. Our data draws on interviews and workshops with 118 logistics and sustainability experts and examines how physical, cyber‐physical, and cyber Industry 4.0T affect sustainability outcomes in logistics. Key environmental and social dimensions identified include resource depletion, carbon emissions, working conditions, service quality, and company reputation, shaped by legislation, societal norms, salience bias, and consumer proximity. We propose an iterative, LCA‐based strategic framework for managerial decision‐making, validated through executive consultations. A real‐world case study of a logistics service provider demonstrates the framework's practical value in reducing adoption barriers and aligning environmental and social priorities with economic goals during I4.0T implementation.

title: Digitalization, Green Innovation, and SME Performance in Emerging Economies: The Mediating Role of Cultural Capability and the Reinforcing Role of HRM Practices
abstract: This study examines how digitalization and green innovation influence perceived firm performance by investigating the mediating role of cultural capability and the moderating role of human resource management (HRM) practices. Drawing on the resource‐based view and absorptive capacity theory, data were collected from 399 SMEs in Ghana using a two‐wave survey design and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM). The findings show that digitalization is positively associated with perceived firm performance, whereas green innovation exhibits no significant direct relationship. Both digitalization and green innovation are positively associated with cultural capability; however, cultural capability is negatively associated with perceived firm performance, resulting in significant negative indirect effects that are contrary to the hypothesized positive mediation.
